findings.source: bioRxiv preprint (PubMed 42239408); background: Nadeau & Bengio 2003 corrected resampled t-test; Dietterich 1998
findings.summary: Performance estimates across CV folds are not independent; naive t-tests on fold scores are invalid (420 simulated scenarios, 4 datasets); proposes SHARP (split-half repeated) test; implementations of Nadeau-Bengio correction exist (R correctR, Python correctipy).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Our abstract says fusion is 'statistically indistinguishable from the train-mean predictor'; any such test must be on recording-level paired residuals (e.g. paired bootstrap or Wilcoxon on |error| per recording), not across LOSO folds.

findings.title: Purged / embargoed cross-validation (Lopez de Prado)
findings.summary: Finance-origin technique: purge training samples whose label windows overlap the test window and add an 'embargo' gap after the test period to break autocorrelation leakage. No physiological/CGM application found in the search.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Provides the name and precedent for our one-hour guard gap on BIG IDEAs ('embargo'); cite to show it is a recognised device rather than ad hoc.

findings.title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods (Collins, Moons, Dhiman et al.)
findings.summary: 27-item checklist; items relevant here: 5a sources of data separately for development and evaluation; 10 how study size was arrived at (separately for development and evaluation); 12a whether data were partitioned; 12c all model-building steps including hyperparameter tuning and internal validation; 12d heterogeneity across clusters; 12e comparing multiple models; 18e data availability; 18f code availability; 23a performance estimates with confidence intervals. Box 1 defines evaluation/test data as distinct from data used to train, tune or select, 'such that there is no overlap in participants between the training and evaluation data'. States the TRIPOD 2015 checklist 'should no longer be used'. The phrase 'data leakage' does not appear in the first ~100k characters read.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The reporting standard reviewers at JBHI/TBME are most likely to invoke for a prediction-model paper; we already satisfy most items but should add a sample-size justification (item 10), CIs (23a), and a completed checklist as supplement.

findings.title: PROBAST+AI: updated quality, risk of bias, and applicability assessment tool for prediction models using regression or artificial intelligence methods (Moons et al.)
findings.summary: Risk-of-bias tool with development (16 signalling questions) and evaluation (18) parts across four domains: participants/data sources, predictors, outcome, analysis.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Lets us self-assess our own study and, more usefully, systematically rate the prior PPG-glucose papers we criticise (analysis domain covers data splitting and overfitting) rather than asserting their flaws informally.

findings.title: CONSORT-AI and DECIDE-AI reporting guidelines
findings.source: CONSORT-AI: Liu et al., BMJ 370:m3164, 2020, DOI 10.1136/bmj.m3164 (also Nat Med 26:1364-1374, 2020); DECIDE-AI: Vasey et al., BMJ 377:e070904, 2022, DOI 10.1136/bmj-2022-070904 (announcement Nat Med 27:186-187, 2021, DOI 10.1038/s41591-021-01229-5); overview https://casrai.org/guides/ai-reporting-guidelines-consort-ai-tripod-ai-decide-ai
findings.summary: CONSORT-AI adds 14 items for randomised trials of AI interventions; DECIDE-AI covers early-stage live clinical evaluation of AI decision support (17 AI-specific items, 28 sub-items, 10 generic). STARD-AI (diagnostic accuracy) was still unpublished per the sources found.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Neither applies directly to an offline retrospective algorithm evaluation; TRIPOD+AI and PROBAST+AI are the applicable instruments. Mention CONSORT-AI/DECIDE-AI only to position where PPG-glucose work sits on the translational pathway (pre-DECIDE-AI).

findings.title: IEEE Research Reproducibility policy (IEEE Author Center) and absence of a JBHI/TBME-specific ML checklist
findings.summary: IEEE-wide guidance encourages authors to share data, code and research outputs (figshare, Zenodo, Dryad recommended); IEEE Access runs a code-review/reproducibility badge. Searches found no JBHI- or TBME-specific reporting checklist for ML on physiological signals; the closest are NERVE-ML (J. Neural Eng.), Demirezen et al.'s EEG-ML reproducibility checklist (Front. Neuroergonomics 2024, 10.3389/fnrgo.2024.1346794) and Kinahan et al. FAccT 2024 on EEG-ML pitfalls.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: We cannot cite a JBHI/TBME checklist; instead state compliance with TRIPOD+AI and NERVE-ML and release code/data on Zenodo per IEEE guidance.

findings.title: Prior cross-subject glucose modelling on the BIG IDEAs dataset
findings.source: Bent et al., original BIG IDEAs study (population leave-one-person-out + personalised models; see PhysioNet 10.13026/aw6y-fc44 and npj Digit Med 2021, PMC8172541); 2025 sciforum ECSA-12 paper on cross-subject distribution shift (https://sciforum.net/paper/26583); 2025 generative-model paper with leave-one-person-out (XGBoost personalised RMSE 4.04 mg/dL)
findings.summary: Bent et al. built population models with leave-one-person-out CV and personalised models from E4 + food logs. A 2025 ECSA paper trained personalised XGBoost on 10 subjects and tested on 5 held-out subjects, finding poor cross-subject transfer. A 2025 generative-model paper reports personalised XGBoost RMSE 4.04 mg/dL in low-data settings, which is implausibly low for 5-min CGM against wrist signals unless the split is temporally leaky.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Our BIG IDEAs section should cite Bent et al. and note that prior personalised results on this dataset (RMSE ~4 mg/dL) were obtained without a stated guard gap, consistent with autocorrelation leakage; our subject-mean null model is the reference those papers lack.

implications: Novelty check: Ramesh et al. (ISWC 2026, DOI 10.1145/3830727.3834821) already show that random window-level splits inflate PPG-glucose results and that Clarke A+B is uninformative without a baseline, using the same Mendeley data as an OOD test. Our paper's defensible novelty is (1) the label-replication artefact in the derivative CSV, which no source found describes, (2) LOSO on the raw Mendeley recordings with null/demographic/feature baselines and multiple seeds, (3) the within-subject chronological-with-guard-gap CGM experiment, and (4) released integrity tests. The Introduction and Related Work must cite Ramesh et al., Mehta et al., Yoshizawa/Ohtsuki, Saeb, Brookshire, Kapoor & Narayanan and NERVE-ML; currently the draft cites none of them, and a reviewer will.

Fix the dataset citation: the Mendeley record 10.17632/37pm7jk7jn (v3, 2023) is credited to Kermani & Esmaeili (Univ. of Science and Technology of Mazandaran), not 'Kumar, Kumar, Chaudhary' as in bibitem ppgdataset2023. Also report the 68-label-files vs 67-signal-files discrepancy and the dataset version used.

Add a 'leakage ladder' table or paragraph with quantified rungs from the literature: EEG AD 99.8%->53.0% (Brookshire), SEED-V 1.00->0.32 (NERVE-ML), PPG-BP SD 8.0->23.1 mmHg (Mehta), PPG-BP r inflated by 0.56/0.40 (Yoshizawa), HAR F1 95->57 (Tello), HAR +10%/+16% (Dehghani), PPG-glucose R2 0.60->-0.04 for ResNet-34 (Ramesh), and our own rung: derivative CSV per-subject oracle MAE 0.07 vs raw-data LOSO. Framing our result as the lowest rung of a known ladder makes it a measurement rather than a complaint.

Name the artefact precisely in Kapoor & Narayanan's taxonomy: subject-wise splitting (fixing L3.2 non-independence) does not detect it because it is a label-construction leak created by flattening a one-to-many join and re-windowing; it is not one of their eight types, which is itself a citable contribution. Consider adding a NERVE-ML-style control: train on the derivative CSV with subject-level label permutation and show the oracle MAE is unchanged.

Strengthen statistics: with 23 subjects, use paired bootstrap confidence intervals on recording-level errors (not fold standard errors) for every MAE/r, and a paired test on per-recording |error| for 'fusion vs train mean'; cite Varoquaux 2018 and the invalid-fold-tests literature (Nadeau-Bengio correction). Report 3 seeds for all networks, not only fusion.

Adopt and attach a completed TRIPOD+AI checklist (items 5a, 10, 12a/c/d/e, 18e/f, 23a are the ones reviewers will look for) and a Kapoor-style model info sheet as supplementary material; state the generalisation level of each experiment using the inter-patient / intra-patient vocabulary of Blanc et al. and NERVE-ML. Cite purged/embargoed CV as precedent for the one-hour guard gap.

Use PROBAST+AI's analysis domain to rate the prior PPG-glucose papers we criticise (Zeynali 2025 segment-level 70/15/15 split and '67 testing subjects'; Soliman 2024 augmentation-before-split and 100% zone A; Chu 2021 random 9:1 split with HbA1c feature; Syamsul & Kim 2026 single 4-subject test set, no null model) in a short table instead of the vague 'several use random window-level splits'.

Add two cheap controls that the specificity literature (Blanc et al.) and Mehta et al. make standard: a white-noise/shuffled-input control, and a demographics-only predictor already present as ridge-demo; present Clarke zone A for the null model in every table (Ramesh: baseline A+B 52-78%; ours: constant predictor zone A fraction).

Tone down the unsupported claim that 'the same column layout appears in other published pipelines' unless a specific paper or notebook can be cited; the only public trace found is the Kaggle dataset/notebook by muhammadyasirsaleem (clean-dataset.csv, 46.76 MB), whose page could not be fetched.
gaps_or_uncertainties: Kaggle dataset page (muhammadyasirsaleem/ppg-signal-with-blood-sugar-level-data) returned 403 and curl was blocked by the permission classifier; row count 844,946, upload date, download counts and any discussion of label errors are unverified. No public critique of the Kaggle derivative was found anywhere.
No source found that previously described the label-cycling / group-mean artefact; absence of evidence in web search is not proof of novelty, but it supports the contribution claim.

Yoshizawa/Ohtsuki IEEE Sensors numbers come from the abstract only (full text paywalled); Hammerla & Ploetz 2015 full text not read (no numbers verified); Tello et al. drop range '5.4-33.6%' in their text does not match my recomputation from their Table II (5.4-38.5).

Ramesh et al. report '>90% in Clarke A+B across all settings' in the abstract, but their Table 2 CEG column shows 39-87%; the column may be zone A only or A+B with different filtering; verify before quoting the percentage.
Mendeley dataset authorship: only the v3 landing page was fetched; v1 (which the draft cites) was not opened, so it is conceivable v1 listed different contributors. Check directly.

TRIPOD+AI full text was read only to ~100k characters; the checklist items quoted are from the visible portion. NERVE-ML checklist items themselves (Section 4) were not in the portion read; the guidance summarised is from Sections 2.1-2.5.
No IEEE JBHI- or TBME-specific ML reporting checklist was found; the conclusion that none exists is based on two searches, not on the journals' author pages.

The term 'leakage ladder' does not appear as a named concept in any source found; the closest formalisations are Ramesh et al.'s four protocols, Mehta et al.'s no/domain/data overlap, Yoshizawa's segment/record/subject, Blanc et al.'s intra-experimentation/intra-patient/inter-patient, and NERVE-ML's instance/trial/session/subject/time grouping.
BIG IDEAs prior work (sciforum 2025, generative-model 2025 paper) was seen only via search snippets; their split protocols and the RMSE 4.04 figure were not verified against full texts.

Several key sources are preprints (Ramesh arXiv version is also published at ISWC 2026; Blanc medRxiv 2026; Zeng bioRxiv; Pith referee report is AI-generated, not peer review) and should be cited as such.

review:clinical.lens: Clinical/physiological relevance: non-diabetic cohorts, glucose ranges, reference-measurement noise and CGM lag, signal representation vs. the physiology it is meant to capture, and what a practitioner would need before believing a negative result.
major_issues: NOT PUBLISHABLE AS-IS IN A TRANSACTIONS VENUE (TBME/JBHI): the paper is an honest negative result on 67 recordings / 23 subjects plus a replication of a null finding on BIG IDEAs that two 2026 preprints have already reported. The fixable-but-fatal items are the citation errors, the missing prior work and the absence of any statistical test behind 'statistically indistinguishable'. Verified from results/subject_cv_*.csv with a subject-level bootstrap (1000 resamples, 23 clusters): 1-D CNN minus train-mean MAE = -1.94 mg/dL [-3.35, -0.74] for seed 0, but -1.18 [-3.00, +0.25] for seed 1 and -0.84 [-2.54, +0.82] for seed 2; per-subject Wilcoxon p = 0.007 / 0.19 / 0.15. Fusion: -0.24 [-1.66, +1.09], +0.08 [-1.53, +1.43], +0.40 [-1.10, +2.03]. The abstract's 'best model is the plain 1-D CNN' rests on one seed. Pooled Pearson r for the LOSO train-mean is -0.59 (results/subject_cv_summary.json, mean_seed0.pearson_r), which shows that pooled r under LOSO is biased and should not be used as the headline evidence of 'signal'.

THE 1-D CNN 'SIGNAL' IS LEVERAGE FROM FOUR RECORDINGS. Mendeley glucose is 88-183 mg/dL with only 4/67 recordings >140 mg/dL and 0 <70 (subject_cv_mean_seed0.csv; subjects 13 and 18 each have a single 183 mg/dL recording). Removing y>140 drops the 1-D CNN r from 0.35/0.31/0.32 to 0.28/0.27/0.24 and the fusion r to -0.03/-0.09/-0.08. The predicted range of the 1-D CNN is 98-137 mg/dL (pred std 9.6 vs y std 18.7). A clinician reads this as 'nothing' either way; the paper should not call r = 0.32 'the only reproducible cross-subject signal' without the cluster-robust CI and the leverage analysis.

REFERENCE-MEASUREMENT NOISE FLOOR IS NEVER STATED, SO 'BEATING THE MEAN' HAS NO CLINICAL ANCHOR. Mendeley labels come from an Accu-Chek Active fingerstick meter (https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/37pm7jk7jn/4); ISO 15197:2013 only requires 95% of meter results within +/-15 mg/dL (<100 mg/dL) or +/-15% (>=100 mg/dL) of a lab reference (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5951056). Dexcom G6 MARD is 9.0-9.9% with a lag of 3.7 +/- 3.1 min vs blood (Welsh et al., J Diabetes Sci Technol 2022, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10899839, citing Calhoun 2018). The subject-mean null on BIG IDEAs already has MARD 12.8% (bigideas_summary.json). The paper must state what MAE/MARD would even be detectable against a reference that is itself ~9-15% noisy, and that FDA-grade targets (MARD <10%, 95% within 15/15) are below the null model on this cohort. Neither 'lag' nor 'interstitial' appears anywhere in ieee_paper.tex (grep confirmed), and the loader uses the 10 s immediately before the CGM timestamp (ppg_data.load_bigideas, run_bigideas_cv --max-per-egv 2) without discussing the interstitial delay.

COHORTS CANNOT ANSWER THE TITLE QUESTION. Both cohorts are non-diabetic (Mendeley: health status not stated by the dataset authors, https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/37pm7jk7jn/4; BIG IDEAs: A1c 5.2-6.4%, age 35-65, abstract describes post-menopausal females, https://physionet.org/content/big-ideas-glycemic-wearable/1.1.3/). On the BIG IDEAs test set 68/8664 readings are <70 mg/dL and 150 are >180 mg/dL; computed from results/bigideas_within_1d_seed0.csv, every model detects 0 of 68 hypoglycaemic and 0 of 150 hyperglycaemic readings and all five models share an identical zone-D of 1.07% (= the 93 readings all predicted at ~110). Correlation of model deviation-from-subject-mean with CGM deviation-from-subject-mean is 0.017 (pred deviation std 9.2 vs CGM deviation std 21.4 mg/dL). The paper reports MAE/MARD only; a clinician wants event-level sensitivity/specificity for hypo/hyper, time-in-range agreement, and at minimum the Parkes/Consensus error grid used by ISO 15197:2013 rather than the 1987 Clarke grid. Also, the Introduction motivates acute tracking with chronic hyperglycaemia mechanisms (erythrocyte deformability, vascular compliance) that are not expected to vary minute-to-minute in a euglycaemic person; the physiological premise and the experiment do not match.

THE SIGNAL REPRESENTATION DISCARDS THE PHYSIOLOGY THROUGH WHICH GLUCOSE COULD PLAUSIBLY ACT, SO THE NEGATIVE RESULT IS ABOUT THE PIPELINE, NOT THE CHANNEL. ppg_data.py: 0.5-8 Hz band-pass, 5-s windows (WIN=320), per-window z-scoring, Mexican-hat scalogram min-max scaled. This removes DC/perfusion amplitude, vasomotion (<0.5 Hz), respiratory modulation and any HRV (needs >= 1-2 min). The published positive results on this very cohort use minute-scale HR/HRV/EDA/temperature features (Bent et al., npj Digit Med 2021, doi:10.1038/s41746-021-00465-w; Karunarathna & Liang, Sensors 2025, doi:10.3390/s25103207, XGBoost MARD 7.1% but no null baseline and split not stated). The npz already holds 60 s of pre-reading BVP (fetch_bigideas.py WIN_PRE=60; load_bigideas lookback_s=60, max_windows_per_egv=12) but the paper uses 10 s (--max-per-egv 2). Empatica E4 BVP is additionally a vendor-processed signal, not raw PPG. The title 'How much glucose information does a single PPG channel carry?' is therefore an overclaim; retitle to what was tested.

NO POSITIVE CONTROL AND NO POWER STATEMENT, WHICH A NEGATIVE-RESULT PAPER CANNOT DO WITHOUT. Nothing shows that the identical windows/protocol can recover ANY known quantity (heart rate, subject identity, time of day, age) under LOSO; without that, 'no model beats the mean' is indistinguishable from 'the pipeline is broken'. With 67 recordings and per-subject error SD on the order of 10 mg/dL, the subject-level bootstrap half-width is ~1.3-1.7 mg/dL, i.e. the experiment could not have detected a clinically modest 1 mg/dL improvement anyway. State the minimal detectable effect.

NO SIGNAL-QUALITY GATING ON FREE-LIVING WRIST DATA. Windows are accepted if finite and std > 1e-3 (ppg_data.load_bigideas); per-subject BVP coverage ranges 0.30-0.95 (data.nosync/bigideas/sub_*_summary.json; subject 015 cov 0.30, n_test 149). Accelerometer is stored in the npz but unused; no SQI, no motion/stillness stratification, no night-vs-day split. A physiologist cannot separate 'no information' from 'no clean signal'. Report the same metrics on ACC-still, high-SQI windows.

CITATION INTEGRITY: SEVERAL REFERENCES ARE WRONG OR UNVERIFIABLE. (a) \bibitem{ppgdataset2023} credits 'D. Kumar, V. Kumar, S. Chaudhary'; the Mendeley record 10.17632/37pm7jk7jn.1 lists Ali Kermani and Hossein Esmaeili, Univ. of Science and Technology of Mazandaran (https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/37pm7jk7jn/1); the paper's '7 female, 16 male, 22-61 years' also disagrees with the dataset authors' own paper (8 F / 15 M, 20-61 y; Kermani & Esmaeili, BioImpacts 2025, doi:10.34172/bi.30589). (b) \bibitem{bigideas2023} 'B. Bent, M. Cho, A. Wittmann et al.' is wrong; PhysioNet's required citation is Cho P, Kim J, Bent B, Dunn J, BIG IDEAs Lab Glycemic Variability and Wearable Device Data (v1.1.3), doi:10.13026/aw6y-fc44, plus Bent et al. npj Digit Med 4:89 (2021). (c) \bibitem{dinh2022ppg} could not be located in any index. (d) \bibitem{li2020ecg} is a sleep-staging CNN-LSTM paper cited as the source for wavelet scalograms of PPG. (e) \bibitem{hina2021noninvasive} key says 2021, entry says 2022 (DOI 10.3390/s22134855 is correct). For IEEE this alone would trigger a reject.

DIRECTLY OVERLAPPING PRIOR WORK IS MISSING, AND IT PRE-EMPTS CONTRIBUTIONS 3 AND 4. (i) Ramesh, Neufeld, Kuettner, Roeddiger, Beigl, 'Reassessing the Feasibility of PPG-Based Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Level Estimation', arXiv:2608.01820 (Aug 2026): five PPG-BGL methods under random / participant-aware / leave-some-participants-out splits -> near-zero or negative R^2 comparable to the mean baseline, and >90% Clarke A+B for every model AND the baseline. That is this paper's Mendeley result and its Clarke-grid argument. (ii) Seyedebrahimi, Ojeda, Zarrintaj, 'A Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Sensor Fusion for Wrist-Worn...', medRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.08.03.26359550 (Aug 2026; code github.com/mirmehdi/physiofusion): BIG IDEAs, subject-grouped CV, wristband-only RMSE 22.58 vs time-of-day 22.63 vs train-mean 22.76 mg/dL; conclusion 'wrist signals carry no glucose information beyond the cohort mean'. That is this paper's contribution 4. (iii) Bent et al. 2021 (87% personalised accuracy on the same cohort) and Karunarathna & Liang 2025 (MARD 7.1%, no null baseline) are the claims this paper should be positioned against, and neither is cited. The paper must re-scope to what remains new: the label-replication artefact, the within-subject chronological guard-gap protocol, and the fusion-vs-1D capacity comparison.

THE 'WIDELY CIRCULATED DERIVATIVE' IS NAMEABLE AND THE INSINUATION ABOUT 'OTHER PUBLISHED MODELS' IS UNSUPPORTED. clean-dataset.csv with columns PPG_Signal / Glucose_Level / Patient_Id is the Kaggle dataset 'PPG signal with Blood sugar level data' (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/muhammadyasirsaleem/ppg-signal-with-blood-sugar-level-data) with companion notebook https://www.kaggle.com/code/muhammadyasirsaleem/predict-blood-glucose-level-using-ppg-signals and repo https://github.com/yasirsaleem502/Predict-Blood-Glucose-Level-Based-on-PPG-Signals, which does not credit Mendeley. Cite it, and either name a peer-reviewed paper that used it or delete 'judging by its column layout, for other published models'. Note the dataset authors' own paper (Kermani & Esmaeili 2025) reports RMSE 26.0 mg/dL together with MAE 4.0 mg/dL and MARD 0.195% under unspecified 5-fold CV, which is internally inconsistent; that is a concrete, citable example for the paper's reporting critique.

BIG IDEAS PROTOCOL GAPS A CLINICIAN WOULD FLAG: (a) a single chronological 70/30 split and one seed (bigideas_summary.json: all within_* entries seed 0) - no blocked/rolling CV, so results depend on which days fell in the last 30%; (b) the fusion row of Table II is '--' (never run; README says 'not in the paper yet') - run it or delete the row; (c) the Dexcom rate-of-change column is 100% NaN in the export (sub_001_dexcom.csv roc), so no stratification by glucose trend, which is where a CGM-lag effect would show; (d) the appropriate comparators for a 'tracking' claim also include persistence (last CGM value: MAE 2.39 mg/dL pooled at 5-min lag, computed from bigideas_within_1d_seed0.csv) and time-of-day (used by Seyedebrahimi et al.); state the intended use-case (calibration-free spot check vs. CGM replacement) so the reader knows which null applies; (e) the text says 'adults without diabetes diagnosis' - PhysioNet states A1c 5.2-6.4% (high-normal to prediabetic), which is clinically different and should be stated as such.

CAPACITY CONFOUND IN THE 'FUSION HURTS' CLAIM: fusion has 548,801 parameters vs ~150k for the 1-D branch on 201 training windows; no capacity-matched 1-D model, no late-fusion/average-of-branches control, no frozen-branch probe. The claim 'adding the 2-D and 3-D views hurts' is confounded with 3.6x more parameters and is anyway inside the bootstrap CI.
minor_issues: Clarke error grid (1987) is obsolete for clinical reviewers; ISO 15197:2013 uses the Parkes/Consensus grid, and the Surveillance Error Grid (Klonoff 2014) is the FDA-era standard. Report at least Parkes zones.

Add the FDA safety communication of 21 Feb 2024 warning against non-invasive smartwatch/ring glucose claims (https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/safety-communications/do-not-use-smartwatches-or-smart-rings-measure-blood-glucose-levels-fda-safety-communication); it is the clinical context that makes a leakage-controlled negative result relevant.

Mendeley measurement protocol: the dataset page says glucometer reading was taken after the PPG recording with no stated gap, no fasting state, index-finger green-LED (550 nm) sensor; state these and that green-LED finger PPG has shallow penetration (a physiological reason to expect little glucose information).

within_subject_r_median in subject_cv_summary.json is meaningless on Mendeley (most subjects have 2-3 recordings, so r is +/-1); it is not in the paper, but delete it from the released JSON or document it.
R^2 'relative to the pooled mean' makes the LOSO train-mean null itself negative (-0.04); explain or use a per-fold definition.

Per-window z-scoring plus min-max scaled scalograms means amplitude/perfusion index is unavailable to every model; say so explicitly in Methods, since perfusion is one of the few PPG quantities with a plausible glucose/insulin (vasodilation) link.
Macro fallbacks (\providecommand ... {--}) mean the compiled PDF can silently show '--' in tables; make the build fail instead.
Table I has an unused leading column and 'multirow' labels; Table II lacks n per subject and a per-subject CGM SD column, which is the quantity the null MAE scales with.
Keywords/abstract say 'statistically indistinguishable' - either add the test or remove the word 'statistically'.
The 'mean' row uses one seed and the networks use three on Mendeley but one on BIG IDEAs; harmonise or justify.
Author block has placeholder affiliation/email; \markboth says 'IEEE Transactions' without naming one - pick the target (JBHI is the natural fit for a methods/negative-result paper).
strengths: Open, honest withdrawal of the earlier 6.89 mg/dL / 98.9% zone-A result with the mechanism (label cycling with period k per subject) explained and an automated test (tests/test_integrity.py::test_clean_dataset_csv_is_a_cross_join) that detects it.

Protocol matches the text: LOSO by subject (sklearn LeaveOneGroupOut on ws.subject), train-only label standardisation (train_fold mu/sd from y[tr]), fixed epochs with no early stopping, recording-level aggregation before metrics, chronological split with a one-hour guard applied on the training side (chronological_split: t < cut - gap_s), subject-mean null for the within-subject protocol. I found no leakage in run_subject_cv.py / run_bigideas_cv.py / ppg_data.py.
All numbers flow from results/*.json via make_results_macros.py; no hand-typed results. Out-of-fold predictions are released, which made the independent re-analysis above possible.
The point that a constant predictor lands 83.6% of recordings in Clarke zone A on a euglycaemic cohort is correct and clinically important (and is corroborated independently by Ramesh et al. 2026).

The Discussion's reporting recommendations (null model, measurement-level metrics, guard gap, zone A next to null, integrity test) are sound and would be useful to the field if the paper were re-scoped as a reporting/reproducibility contribution.
what_would_change_my_verdict: Add a positive control under the identical pipeline and LOSO/chronological protocol (e.g. heart rate or subject identity from the same windows) proving the pipeline can find a signal; add a minimal-detectable-effect statement from the subject-level bootstrap.

Replace 'statistically indistinguishable' with subject-clustered bootstrap CIs and paired per-subject tests for every model-vs-null comparison, over >= 3 seeds on both datasets, and report the y<=140 leverage analysis; drop pooled Pearson r under LOSO or report it with the null's r = -0.59.

Fix every reference (Kermani & Esmaeili for Mendeley; Cho/Kim/Bent/Dunn for PhysioNet; remove or replace dinh2022ppg and li2020ecg) and cite + position against Ramesh et al. arXiv:2608.01820, Seyedebrahimi et al. medRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.03.26359550, Bent et al. 2021, Karunarathna & Liang 2025, Kermani & Esmaeili 2025; name the Kaggle derivative explicitly.

Retitle and re-scope: the artefact report + guard-gap within-subject protocol + capacity-matched fusion-vs-1D comparison are the novel parts; the title must not claim to measure 'how much information a PPG channel carries'.

Add the clinical frame: reference noise (ISO 15197 meter limits, G6 MARD 9-9.9%, lag 3.7 +/- 3.1 min), cohort A1c status, hypo/hyper event sensitivity (currently 0/68 and 0/150), Parkes/Consensus grid, and an explicit statement of the intended use-case with persistence and time-of-day nulls alongside subject-mean.

Use the available 60 s of pre-reading BVP with amplitude retained and an SQI/accelerometer stillness gate, with a sensitivity analysis over window length, so the negative result is not attributable to a 5-s, DC-stripped representation.
Either run the fusion network on BIG IDEAs (several seeds, several chronological cut points or blocked CV) or remove the dashed table row; harmonise seeds across datasets.

sweep:datasets.angle: DATASETS: every public dataset pairing PPG/wrist BVP (or near-substitutes) with reference glucose or CGM; access terms, size, cohort, sensors, glucose range, diabetes status, and laptop-feasibility within days. Also two concurrent 2026 leakage-controlled null-result papers found while checking datasets, because they change the novelty claim.

findings.title: BIG IDEAs Lab Glycemic Variability and Wearable Device Data v1.1.3 (PhysioNet) — ALREADY USED
findings.source: https://physionet.org/content/big-ideas-glycemic-wearable/1.1.3/ ; DOI 10.13026/aw6y-fc44 ; original study Bent et al. npj Digit Med 2021 DOI 10.1038/s41746-021-00465-w
findings.summary: Access: OPEN (no credentialing), Open Data Commons Attribution v1.0; must cite dataset + Bent 2021. Size: 4.7 GB zip / 34.1 GB uncompressed (zip already at data.nosync/bigideas/bigideas-1.1.3.zip, 5.0 GB, and 16 per-subject .npz extracts exist locally). Subjects: 16 adults, age 35–65, point-of-care HbA1c 5.2–6.4% (prediabetes range, no diabetes diagnosis); PhysioNet abstract also says 'only post-menopausal females' while the data description says 'elevated glucose in normal range' — sex criterion ambiguous. Duration: 8–10 days free-living. Sensors: Empatica E4 (BVP 64 Hz, EDA + skin temp 4 Hz, ACC 32 Hz, HR 1 Hz derived), Dexcom G6 CGM every 5 min, food logs (v1.1.0+; v1.1.3 fixed misaligned food-log dates). OGTT files were corrupted and omitted. Glucose range: not stated on page; repo macros give 46–261 mg/dL over 8664 held-out readings. Dates time-shifted.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Already the within-subject dataset. Note the version history (v1.1.2 → v1.1.3 changed food logs only) and that a concurrent medRxiv 2026 paper (see 'PhysioFusion' finding) ran a leakage-controlled fusion study on v1.1.2 and reached the same wrist-only ≈ mean-predictor conclusion.

findings.title: Mendeley 'PPG signals collected from a pulse sensor to measure blood glucose level' (a.k.a. MUST dataset) — ALREADY USED; AUTHOR CITATION IN DRAFT IS WRONG
findings.source: https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/37pm7jk7jn/1 (v1, 26 Jun 2023, DOI 10.17632/37pm7jk7jn.1) ; https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/37pm7jk7jn/4 (v4, 10 Sep 2025, DOI 10.17632/37pm7jk7jn.4) ; IEEE DataPort mirror DOI 10.21227/mekr-0a81 (subscription-only, 13 Dec 2024)
findings.summary: Contributors on every version and on IEEE DataPort: Ali Kermani and Hossein Esmaeili, University of Science and Technology of Mazandaran, Iran — NOT 'D. Kumar, V. Kumar, S. Chaudhary' as cited in ieee_paper.tex line 545 and text line 181. Access: OPEN, CC BY 4.0, ~2.8 MB zip. 67 raw PPG signals from 23 volunteers, 10 s each at 2175 Hz, 12-bit ADC, fingertip green-LED (550 nm, APDS-9008) pulse sensor; reference glucose by Accu-Chek Active fingerstick (mg/dL); labels carry ID, sex, age, height, weight. Labels folder has 68 files vs 67 signals (unexplained on all versions). v4 adds .csv next to .mat. Diabetes status and glucose range are NOT stated on the page (repo computes 88–183 mg/dL, mean 115; Ramesh et al. 2026 report the same 88–183, M=115.01, SD=18.67). Ramesh et al. 2026 call it 'MUST'. Re-uploads exist on Kaggle ('PPG Glucose Dataset', mhamza1018, CC0, Figures/Labels/RawData, ~9.9 MB; and 'PPG signal with Blood sugar level data', muhammadyasirsaleem, containing a clean-dataset.csv of ~46.76 MB — plausibly the corrupted derivative, but Kaggle pages are JS-rendered and could not be read).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: (1) Fix bibitem ppgdataset2023 to Kermani & Esmaeili and cite the exact version used (loader reads Archive_Dataset/archive (2)/PPG_Dataset with .csv files, i.e. v3/v4 layout, while the bib says v1). (2) The draft calls the cohort 'non-diabetic' (Limitations, line ~493) — the dataset page never states this; with values up to 183 mg/dL this should be softened to 'diabetes status not reported'. (3) If the Kaggle clean-dataset.csv is the artefact source, naming the public location strengthens the artefact section; needs manual check in a browser.

findings.title: PhysioCGM: multimodal physiological dataset for non-invasive blood glucose estimation (Texas A&M PSI lab; Scientific Data 2025)
findings.source: Paper DOI 10.1038/s41597-025-06090-6 (Sci Data 12:1822, 19 Nov 2025; PMC12630648) ; data: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28136294 (springernature.figshare) ; code: https://github.com/PSI-TAMU/PhysioCGM
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC0 1.0, no embargo, direct figshare download. Size: 25.0 GB total = 10 raw zips (0.79–1.02 GB each, c1s01–c2s05) + 10 processed zips (1.3–1.9 GB each, .pkl 5-min clips aligned to CGM timestamps, split by day). Subjects: 10 adults with Type 1 diabetes, two cohorts of 5. Duration: up to 17 days ambulatory. Sensors: Empatica E4 (raw PPG/BVP, EDA, skin temp, ACC — E4 BVP is 64 Hz by device spec; GitHub does not restate), Zephyr BioHarness (ECG 250 Hz 12-bit, breathing 25 Hz, ACC), Dexcom G6 CGM (5 min). Glucose range: not given on figshare/GitHub; paper tags include hypoglycemia. Companion work from the same lab (Tseng et al. 2025, J Diabetes Sci Technol DOI 10.1177/19322968251319347) predicts hypoglycemia from ECG beats.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The single most useful addition: it is the only open dataset with raw wrist PPG + CGM in a DIABETIC cohort, directly answering the draft's limitation that both cohorts are non-diabetic. Same E4/Dexcom G6 hardware as BIG IDEAs, so ppg_data.py's BIG IDEAs loader (64 Hz BVP, 5-min CGM) should port with minimal change. Download the 10 raw zips (~9.2 GB) or the processed pkls; feasible on a laptop in a day.

findings.title: STUBA ePPG 'Photoplethysmography (PPG) Dataset for Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Monitoring' (Berki & Mateasik, Slovak Univ. of Technology; Zenodo)
findings.source: Concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21308261 ; versions: 10.5281/zenodo.21308262 (v1, 11 Jul 2026), 10.5281/zenodo.21978226 (v1.1.1, 17 Aug 2026, adds qc_channels.csv/qc_records.csv), 10.5281/zenodo.22206256 (v1.2.0, 31 Aug 2026, adds code zip)
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC0 1.0. Size: ~6 MB (stuba_ppg_bgl_dataset.zip 5.9 MB). Subjects: 24 volunteers — 21 healthy controls + 3 with T1DM. Records: 125, each trimmed to 30 s. Sensor: in-house six-channel ePPG device (two photodiodes × green 530 / red 655 / IR 940 nm) at 100 Hz plus tri-axial accelerometer. Reference: Beurer GL49 capillary fingerstick (mmol/L, in .atr annotation files), taken ≤1 min before PPG. Glucose range: not stated numerically ('normal to significant glycemic excursions'). Device design paper DOI 10.1109/ASDAM55965.2022.9966768.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: A second Mendeley-style set (few recordings per subject, fingerstick reference) with 3 wavelengths; ideal for a LOSO replication of the 'no model beats train-mean' result and for a per-wavelength ablation. Trivial to download and run (<10 MB).

findings.title: IIIT-Delhi Empatica EmbracePlus + FreeStyle Libre paired dataset ('An Exploratory Study of Blood Glucose Estimation from PPG Signals using Machine Learning')
findings.source: Data: https://zenodo.org/records/20577959 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20577959, v1 7 Jun 2026; page says a newer version exists) ; paper arXiv:2606.15927 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15927)
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY 4.0. Size: Data.zip 3.5 GB + Paper.pdf. Subjects: 5 volunteers (3 M, 2 F); diabetes status not stated. Duration: 14 days each (~1,680 h total). Sensors: Empatica EmbracePlus wrist PPG at 64 Hz; FreeStyle Libre CGM at 15-min intervals (mmol/L). Glucose range: not reported. Authors' own results: within-subject temporal split MLP MAPE ~11%; Clarke 73.6% zone A but 25.6% zone E; no null-model baseline reported.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Small but free-living wrist PPG + CGM on a consumer-style successor to the E4. Usable as an external within-subject tracking check (5 subjects) with the BIG IDEAs protocol; the authors did not test a subject-mean baseline, which our protocol would supply.

findings.title: VitalDB (Seoul National University Hospital surgical database) — PPG waveform + laboratory/preoperative glucose
findings.source: PhysioNet mirror https://physionet.org/content/vitaldb/1.0.0/ (DOI 10.13026/czw8-9p62, CC BY 4.0, 95.4 GB) ; web API https://api.vitaldb.net/labs and https://vitaldb.net/dataset/?query=api ; AWS Open Data https://registry.opendata.aws/vitaldb/ ; original paper Lee et al. Sci Data 2022 9:279
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY 4.0 (PhysioNet page says anyone may download subject to licence; AWS registry lists CC BY 4.0). 6,388 surgical cases (~6,090 patients); PLETH waveform from the TramRac-4A monitor (Ramesh et al. report 500 Hz); clinical_parameters.csv includes preop_gluc (EMR, mg/dL) and lab_data.csv holds 34 time-series lab parameters within ±90 days of anaesthesia start. Ramesh et al. 2026 obtained PPG+glucose pairs for 4,872 cases / 4,626 unique patients, glucose 44–525 mg/dL (M 117.2, SD 44.3). Diabetes status: available only via EMR fields, not a design variable; patients are under anaesthesia (confound). Per-case tracks can be pulled selectively through the vitaldb Python API, so the full 95 GB is not required.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The only PPG–glucose resource with thousands of subjects. Ramesh et al. (arXiv:2608.01820) already show that five published PPG→glucose methods collapse to the mean baseline under participant-aware/LSPO splits on it (mean-baseline MAE 26.4 mg/dL, R²≈0). Running the 1D/2D/3D fusion network under the same LSPO protocol would scale the draft's claim from 23 to ~4,600 subjects, but anaesthesia/surgical confounds must be acknowledged.

findings.title: Hb-PPG: four-wavelength PPG dataset with hemoglobin, fasting glucose and BP (CardioWorks/Guilin; Scientific Data 2026)
findings.source: Paper DOI 10.1038/s41597-026-06945-6 (Sci Data 13:564, 2026; PMC13066573) ; data https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.22256143 (v7, 10 Aug 2026, Hb_PPG_Dataset.zip 46.8 MB) ; code https://github.com/CardioWorks/Hemoglobin-Dataset-2025-main
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY 4.0 on figshare (S2 metadata lists CC BY-NC-ND for the article). 1,008 PPG segments at 660/730/850/940 nm from 252 adults (267 recorded, 15 excluded for invalid signals), with reference hemoglobin, FASTING blood glucose and brachial SBP/DBP. Sampling rate, segment length, glucose range and diabetes status were not retrievable from figshare/GitHub (the earlier v1 of the same figshare record was a 58-subject, 200 Hz, 60-s set — do not confuse). Designed for Hb, glucose is a secondary label.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Largest open finger-PPG set with a glucose label per subject (one fasting value each → cross-subject only). Good for a 252-subject LOSO/grouped-CV replication of the cross-subject null result; download is 47 MB.

findings.title: Jilin University 183-participant longitudinal finger-PPG + capillary glucose benchmark (arXiv:2607.04414) — NOT yet downloadable
findings.summary: 183 participants (112 M/71 F; 31% diabetic at enrolment; mean age 57), 1–5 encounters each over 285 days (Mar 2024–Jan 2025), 10-min sessions, Analog Devices ADPD4100 finger PPG at 1 kHz, Accu-Chek Performa reference, observed range 4.2–16.3 mmol/L (mean 6.56±2.12); 5,224 non-overlapping 4-s windows (4,104 non-diabetic, 1,120 diabetic). Access: 'controlled-access repository upon submission of a completed access request form'; repository details withheld until acceptance. Reported subject-independent 5-fold MAE 0.64 mmol/L (~11.5 mg/dL), RMSE 1.29 mmol/L, zone A 83.6–91.1%; no mean-predictor baseline reported.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Shows the field is producing larger diabetic finger-PPG cohorts, but it cannot be obtained within days. Their SD of 2.12 mmol/L (~38 mg/dL) implies a mean predictor would give MAE roughly 25–30 mg/dL, so their 11.5 mg/dL would be a real effect if it holds — worth citing as the strongest counter-evidence and as a target for replication once released.

findings.title: D1NAMO (HES-SO Valais; Zenodo) — ECG/respiration/accelerometer + glucose, NO PPG
findings.source: https://zenodo.org/records/5651217 (v1.2.0, mirror of https://zenodo.org/record/1421615) ; paper Dubosson et al. 2018, Informatics in Medicine Unlocked 13:92–100, DOI 10.1016/j.imu.2018.09.003 ; preprocessing code https://github.com/PSI-TAMU/D1NAMO
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY-SA 4.0, 10.2 GB in six zips (diabetes ECG 1.7 GB, diabetes sensor 1.1 GB, diabetes pictures/glucose/food/insulin 252 MB, healthy ECG 4.1 GB, healthy sensor 2.6 GB, healthy pictures/glucose/food 477 MB). 20 healthy + 9 T1D subjects, Zephyr BioHarness 3 chest strap (ECG 250 Hz 12-bit, breathing, accelerometer), glucose measurements (CGM for the T1D subset per the TAMU preprocessing repo, converted to mg/dL; device model not stated on Zenodo), annotated food pictures, insulin for T1D. Per-subject duration not stated on the Zenodo page (commonly described as ~4 days each — unverified here). No optical/PPG channel.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Not usable for the PPG hypothesis. Only relevant if the paper generalises to 'single physiological channel vs CGM' (ECG analogue).

findings.title: OhioT1DM (Marling & Bunescu, 2018/2020) — CGM + fitness-band aggregates, NO raw PPG
findings.summary: Access: ON REQUEST — email the maintainer with institutional email, name, title, institution/address; ~1 week; encrypted archive + password; a Data Use Agreement signed by institution legal signatories is required (paper §5). 12 adults with T1D, 8 weeks each, Medtronic 530G/630G pumps, Medtronic Enlite CGM every 5 min, fingersticks, insulin, meals, life events. Physiological data: 2018 cohort (IDs 559,563,570,575,588,591) Basis Peak — heart rate, GSR, skin temp, air temp, steps as 5-min aggregates; 2020 cohort (540,544,552,567,584,596) Empatica Embrace — GSR, skin temp, acceleration magnitude as 1-min aggregates, NO heart rate. No raw PPG/BVP anywhere. Dates shifted; XML format.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Answers the task's 'has it any PPG? check' — No. At most a 5-min HR series for six subjects. Not suitable for this paper; cite only when discussing CGM-forecasting literature.

findings.title: ShanghaiT1DM and ShanghaiT2DM (Zhao et al., Scientific Data 2023) — CGM + clinical/diet, NO wearable or PPG
findings.source: Paper DOI 10.1038/s41597-023-01940-7 (PMC9849330) ; figshare collection https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.6310860 ; records 10.6084/m9.figshare.20444397.v3 (data.zip 3.4 MB, 20 Nov 2022) and 10.6084/m9.figshare.21600933.v5 (diabetes_datasets.zip 3.7 MB, 30 Oct 2023)
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY 4.0 on figshare, ~3.5 MB. 12 T1D (16 files, 15,695 CGM points) and 100 T2D patients (109 files, 112,475 points), CGM every 15 min for 3–14 days, plus capillary glucose, ketones, dietary records (3/day), insulin, medications, labs, clinical characteristics. No PPG, heart rate or any wearable channel.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Not usable for PPG→glucose. Useful only as a CGM-statistics reference for diabetic glucose variability (contrast with the 80–140 mg/dL argument in the Discussion).

findings.title: CGMacros (PhysioNet, Jan 2025) — dual CGM + Fitbit Sense heart rate, NO raw PPG
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, 628 MB. 45 participants (15 healthy HbA1c<5.7, 16 prediabetes 5.7–6.4, 14 T2D >6.4), 10 days free-living with designed breakfasts/lunches. FreeStyle Libre Pro (15 min) + Dexcom G6 Pro (5 min) CGMs, Fitbit Sense giving 1-min average heart rate (bpm) only, meal macronutrients/photos, microbiome. Per-participant files at 1-min resolution.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: No PPG waveform, so cannot test the hypothesis; could serve a 'heart-rate-only' control if the paper ever argues that PPG-derived HR carries the information.

findings.title: AI-READI / Bridge2AI (FAIRhub) — 1,067 participants, Dexcom G6 + Garmin Vivosmart 5, NO raw PPG
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.2 ; docs https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/2/dataset/wearable-activity-monitor/ (v2; v3.0.0 is current) ; summary https://hivelab.biochemistry.gwu.edu/wiki/AI-READI_Dataset_Overview
findings.summary: Access: CONTROLLED — custom University of Washington data licence; request via FAIRhub with data-type selection, typically approved within days (per Retinal Physician 2025); Glucose-ML lists it as controlled. 1,067 adults across the T2D spectrum (normal → insulin-treated T2D), ~10 days Dexcom G6 (5 min) and Garmin Vivosmart 5 at 5-s sampling providing heart rate (bpm, optical), stress, SpO2 (sleep only), respiratory rate, steps, calories, sleep stages — as Open mHealth JSON. Raw PPG is not exported from the Garmin.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Largest wearable+CGM cohort but only derived HR, not BVP; could support a future 'does any wrist-derived series beat the subject mean' analysis, not the present PPG-view study.

findings.title: T1DEXI / T1DEXIP (Jaeb Center; Vivli) — 497 adults with T1D, CGM + heart rate, controlled access
findings.summary: Access: CONTROLLED via Vivli data request/DUA (BrisT1D paper marks it 'not openly accessible'). 497 adults with T1D, 4 weeks, structured exercise sessions, CGM, insulin, diet, heart rate (a Vivli request by Verily names the Study Watch; the data dictionary was not retrievable, so raw PPG availability is unconfirmed and unlikely). Pediatric T1DEXIP is separate.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Not obtainable within days; heart-rate only as far as could be determined.

findings.title: HUPA-UCM Diabetes Dataset (Mendeley Data, Data in Brief 2024) — FreeStyle Libre 2 + Fitbit Ionic, NO raw PPG
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY 4.0. 25 people with T1D (22 in the MetaboNet consolidation), ≥14 days, FreeStyle Libre 2 CGM (15 min), Fitbit Ionic steps/calories/heart rate/sleep. No waveform data.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Not usable for PPG; HR-only.

findings.title: BUT CGM: Brno University of Technology Continuous Glycaemia, ECG, Activity and Food Intake Database (PhysioNet, 2 Nov 2026) — ECG not PPG
findings.summary: Access: OPEN, CC BY 4.0, 59.4 GB zip / 60.5 GB. 60 healthy sporting adults (65 records; ages 20–46; 18 F/42 M), ~10 days free-living, Dexcom G7 CGM (5 min), Bittium Faros 180 single-lead ECG at 1 kHz + 3-axis ACC 100 Hz, sports-watch activity/sleep logs, food intake. No PPG sensor; HR derived from ECG.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Not PPG; could be the ECG analogue of the BIG IDEAs experiment (healthy, non-diabetic) if the paper broadens scope. Too large to be worth downloading for this submission.

findings.title: MIMIC-IV-Ext-ECG-Glucose (PhysioNet, 6 Oct 2026) and MIMIC-III waveform — waveform-to-lab-glucose pairing pattern, credentialed
findings.summary: Access: CREDENTIALED (PhysioNet training + DUA; typically 1–2 weeks). 437,671 lab-glucose/12-lead-ECG pairs from 131,771 patients, matched within ±240 min. ECG only — no PPG. The MIMIC-III waveform matched subset (credentialed, very large) contains PLETH and could be paired with lab glucose the same way; one 2026 study (ResNet+Transformer, PMC12838076) claims to have done so, but its pairing details could not be read (PMC blocked).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Shows the ±240-min lab-pairing convention; not feasible within days and ICU glucose sampling is care-driven, so not recommended for this paper.

findings.title: Ramesh, Neufeld, Küttner, Röddiger, Beigl — 'Reassessing the Feasibility of PPG-Based Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Level Estimation' (KIT; arXiv Aug 2026) — concurrent null-result paper using VitalDB + MUST(Mendeley)
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01820 (3 Aug 2026; an ACM DOI 10.1145/3830727.3834821 appeared in search results but could not be verified via arXiv metadata)
findings.summary: Re-implements five published PPG→glucose methods (Zeynali 2025 ResNet-34; Alghlayini 2023 1D-CNN; Prabha 2022 MFCC+XGBoost; Islam 2021 PLS; Gupta 2021 XGBoost) on VitalDB (4,626 participants, 500 Hz) and MUST/Mendeley (23 subjects, 88–183 mg/dL). Random window split: ResNet-34 MAE 13.97, R² 0.60. Participant-aware / leave-some-participants-out: every model R² ≈ 0 or negative (ResNet LSPO MAE 25.93 vs mean-baseline 26.39 mg/dL); OOD (train VitalDB → test MUST) all models ≈ mean baseline (16.0 mg/dL). >90% Clarke A+B for every model including the mean predictor; they conclude zone metrics hide failure.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Directly overlapping conclusion published ~3 months before this draft. Must be cited. Our distinct contributions remain: (a) the label-replication artefact in the public derivative, (b) the 1D/2D/3D fusion vs single-branch ablation, (c) the within-subject CGM tracking with guard gap. Their VitalDB numbers also give a ready external benchmark.

findings.title: PhysioFusion — Seyedebrahimi, Ojeda, Zarrintaj, 'A Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Sensor Fusion for Wrist-Worn Glucose Estimation' (medRxiv Aug 2026) — concurrent null result on BIG IDEAs
findings.summary: Uses BIG IDEAs v1.1.2 (15 participants), 5-fold subject-grouped CV with automated leakage tests, 30-min-ahead glucose forecasting. RMSE (mg/dL): CGM-history linear 13.90; CGM + wrist summary features 13.56–13.60 (no gain); early-fusion TCN CGM+wrist 14.66–14.68; wristband-only 22.58; time-of-day-only 22.63; training-mean 22.76. Conclusion: 'sensor fusion cannot recover information the sensor does not acquire'.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Second concurrent paper reaching the same wrist-only ≈ null conclusion on the same dataset. Must be cited and differentiated: they forecast with CGM history and summary features; we estimate from raw BVP windows with a subject-mean null and a chronological guard gap. Their time-of-day baseline is a good idea to add to our BIG IDEAs table.

implications: Downloadable and runnable on a laptop within days (raw PPG + glucose, open licence): PhysioCGM (25 GB total, ~9 GB raw zips, CC0, 10 T1D adults, E4 BVP + Dexcom G6) — the top addition because it is the only open DIABETIC wrist-PPG/CGM cohort; STUBA ePPG (6 MB, CC0, 24 subjects, 3 wavelengths, fingerstick) and Hb-PPG (47 MB, CC BY, 252 subjects, one fasting glucose each) for cheap cross-subject replications; IIIT-Delhi EmbracePlus+Libre (3.5 GB, CC BY, 5 subjects, 14 days) for a second within-subject tracking check; VitalDB (open CC BY, pull PLETH + preop_gluc per case via the vitaldb API; ~4,600 patients) for scale under LSPO. Mendeley v4 (3 MB) and BIG IDEAs (already local) are in hand.

Datasets that look relevant but carry NO raw PPG and therefore cannot test the paper's question: OhioT1DM (HR/GSR aggregates, DUA by email), D1NAMO (ECG), ShanghaiT1DM/T2DM (CGM only), CGMacros (Fitbit HR), HUPA-UCM (Fitbit HR), AI-READI (Garmin HR, controlled licence), T1DEXI (HR, Vivli DUA), BUT CGM (ECG), MIMIC-IV-Ext-ECG-Glucose (ECG, credentialed). The Jilin 183-subject benchmark (arXiv 2607.04414) is controlled-access and unreleased.

Correct the Mendeley citation now: the dataset authors are Ali Kermani and Hossein Esmaeili (University of Science and Technology of Mazandaran), on every version and on the IEEE DataPort mirror; 'Kumar, Kumar, Chaudhary' is wrong in both the bibliography and the text. Cite the version actually loaded (the loader reads .csv signals, which exist only from v3/v4) and mention the 68-label/67-signal mismatch. Also drop or qualify the claim that the Mendeley cohort is 'non-diabetic' — the dataset never states diabetes status.

Novelty check for an IEEE Transactions submission: two independent 2026 preprints (Ramesh et al., arXiv 2608.01820, VitalDB+MUST under LSPO; Seyedebrahimi et al., medRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.03.26359550, BIG IDEAs leakage-controlled fusion) already report that PPG/wrist models do not beat a mean predictor. The draft is not alone in its conclusion, so the paper must position itself on what is new: the documented label-replication artefact in a circulating derivative, the 1D/2D/3D fusion-vs-single-view ablation, the guard-gap chronological protocol, and (if added) the first leakage-controlled evaluation on a diabetic wrist-PPG cohort (PhysioCGM) plus a 4,600-patient VitalDB LSPO run of the same architecture.

Protocol additions suggested by the dataset survey: add a time-of-day-only baseline on BIG IDEAs (PhysioFusion found it equal to the mean predictor), report MARD and R² alongside Clarke zones (both concurrent papers show >90% A+B for the null model), and state every dataset's licence (ODC-By, CC BY 4.0, CC0) and version in a reproducibility table.
gaps_or_uncertainties: Kaggle pages are JS-rendered and could not be read: whether 'PPG signal with Blood sugar level data' (uploader muhammadyasirsaleem, clean-dataset.csv ~46.76 MB) is the corrupted 844,946-row derivative used in the withdrawn draft must be confirmed in a browser; if so it should be named as the artefact source.

PhysioCGM: E4 BVP sampling rate, glucose range and exact per-subject days were not stated on figshare/GitHub (paper PDF behind a nature.com cookie redirect and PMC captcha); E4 BVP is 64 Hz by device specification.

Hb-PPG: sampling rate, segment length, glucose range and diabetes status were not retrievable (figshare description omits them; GitHub repo holds only SNR scripts). The same figshare record's v1 was a different 58-subject set — verify v7 contents after download.

D1NAMO: per-subject duration (commonly cited as ~4 days) and CGM model (commonly cited as Medtronic iPro2) were not confirmed from Zenodo or abstract pages (ScienceDirect/HES-SO pages returned 403/redirect loops).

VitalDB: the 500 Hz PLETH rate and the 4,872-case PPG+glucose overlap come from Ramesh et al. 2026, not from VitalDB documentation (the vitaldb.net dataset page is a 660k-character single page that could not be parsed); PhysioNet page confirms open CC BY 4.0 and preop_gluc exists in clinical_parameters.csv.

BIG IDEAs inclusion criterion: the PhysioNet abstract text mentions 'only post-menopausal females' while the data description does not; sex composition of the 16 subjects should be checked in the local demographics file before describing the cohort.
T1DEXI: whether the heart-rate series comes from the Verily Study Watch and whether any raw optical data exists could not be verified (Vivli data dictionary not accessible).
arXiv 2608.01820 (Ramesh et al.): a conference DOI 10.1145/3830727.3834821 surfaced in search results but arXiv metadata lists no journal_ref; cite the arXiv version unless verified.

ShanghaiT1DM/T2DM has two figshare records (20444397 v3 and 21600933 v5) in collection c.6310860 with slightly different zip sizes; which is canonical was not determined (irrelevant to this paper since neither has PPG).

PPG-BP (Guilin, figshare, 219 subjects, Liang et al. Sci Data 2018) and BrisT1D (24 UK young adults with smartwatches, arXiv 2507.17757) were noted but excluded: PPG-BP carries a diabetes diagnosis label with no glucose value, and BrisT1D's access terms and signal list could not be established.

sweep:venue.angle: VENUE FIT: negative-result / benchmark / data-artefact papers across IEEE TBME, JBHI, TIM, Sensors J, Access, OJEMB, Physiological Measurement and npj Digital Medicine, plus the 2026 prior-art landscape that now surrounds the paper's three contributions (artefact characterisation, leakage-controlled null benchmark on 23+16 subjects, released code/tests).

findings.title: IEEE Access scope explicitly names negative results; 20% stated acceptance; direct precedent paper (Costa et al. 2023)
findings.source: https://ieeeaccess.ieee.org/about/ ; https://ieeeaccess.ieee.org/authors/ ; Costa et al., IEEE Access 11:57934-57950 (2023), DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3284458 ; https://peeref.com/journals/10017
findings.summary: Official About page scope: 'Applied engineering articles discussing new experiments or measurement techniques, interesting solutions to engineering, including negative results.' Authors page: 'average acceptance rate of 20%', 'Submission to Online Publication 4 to 6 weeks', APC-funded gold OA, peer review assesses 'originality and technical correctness' (third-party sites quote 27%). Precedent: Costa et al. 2023 'Blood Pressure Estimation From Photoplethysmography by Considering Intra- and Inter-Subject Variabilities: Guidelines for a Fair Assessment' showed PPG-BP models score worse on unseen subjects and that a demographics-only regressor matched intra-subject results, i.e. models were identifying individuals, not predicting BP. OpenAlex ISSN-filtered search 2022-2026 finds 19 PPG+glucose items in Access (QU-GM wristband 139 subjects, 2024 scoping review DOI 10.1109/access.2024.3508467, dual-channel ring pilot 2025).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Only venue in the list whose written scope invites negative results; no subject-count threshold; a methodology-critique PPG paper has already been published there. Highest acceptance probability, lowest prestige of the IEEE set.

findings.title: IEEE JBHI: 14-page limit incl. supplementary, mandatory overlength charges above 8 pages, dataset-paper type, 14.9% acceptance; it is the home of the positive PPG-glucose claims the paper refutes
findings.source: https://embs.org/jbhi/prepare-and-submit-your-manuscript ; https://www.embs.org/jbhi/statistics/ ; Ali et al. JBHI 29(7):4692-4702 (2024) DOI 10.1109/jbhi.2024.3464098 ; Li et al. JBHI 29(8):5465-5478 (2025) DOI 10.1109/jbhi.2025.3556666
findings.summary: Author page: 'The page limit is 14 pages for regular papers and 16 pages for review papers including supplementary material'; mandatory $250/page for pages 9-10 and $350/page from page 11 ('not negotiable or voluntary'); 'IEEE J-BHI accepts a new type of papers, which describe a dataset' (must detail construction/annotation; ML models optional); Communications no longer published; no statement on negative results or benchmarks. Statistics page: 'acceptance rate for papers submitted in the last 12 months of 14.9%', submission-to-e-publication < 26 weeks. OpenAlex finds 10 PPG+glucose items 2022-2026, including Ali et al. 2024 (multi-view attention + cascaded BiLSTM, 21 participants, up to 6 days, RMSE 1.67 mmol/L, MARD 17.88%, 98.8% Clarke A+B) and Li et al. 2025 (multi-wavelength PPG, 254 participants, 26,063 measurements, 91.8% Parkes zone A). The Ali 2024 model ('CBHFF') is one of the three models Shen et al. re-evaluate at NeurIPS 2026.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: JBHI has accepted n=21 PPG-glucose deep-learning studies, so small n is not disqualifying; a leakage-controlled refutation plus artefact report is squarely on-topic and 14 pages fits three contributions. Risk: reviewers drawn from the positive-result community and 14.9% acceptance; the paper must present the harness/benchmark as a reusable contribution, not only a null.

findings.title: IEEE TBME: 'novel engineering methods with demonstrated biomedical significance', 8-page regular papers, Letters 'reserved for exceptionally novel works', ~19% acceptance; publishes evaluation critiques only as large reviews
findings.source: https://www.embs.org/tbme/for-authors/ ; https://www.embs.org/tbme/for-authors/prepare-and-submit-manuscript/ ; https://www.embs.org/tbme/?p=65 ; Cheung et al., IEEE TBME 71(12):3569-3592 (2024) DOI 10.1109/TBME.2024.3434344 (PMC11799359)
findings.summary: Aims/scope page: limits 'Regular paper – eight pages; Communication – three pages; Letter – four pages; Review paper – ten pages', mandatory overlength fee ($250/page first two, then $350), EiC permission needed beyond 12 pages, conclusion <= 300 words; scope 'novel engineering methods with demonstrated biomedical significance'; 'LETTERS are reserved for exceptionally novel works'. EiC New Year message (2018) reported 18.7% acceptance (c. 20% in 2017, 22% in 2013). No negative-results or benchmark policy found. The one recent evaluation-critique in TBME is Cheung et al. 2024, a 70-study systematic review + meta-analysis of wearable BP: '42% of the studies performed record splits without personalization and, therefore, suffered from data leakage', 'only 27% of the studies reported sufficient power', 'Many datasets ... have less than 50 subjects'; proposes 'explained deviation' (ED=1 means no better than predicting the mean) and an open-contribution benchmark. OpenAlex 2022-2026 PPG+glucose search in TBME returns no glucose-from-PPG primary paper.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: TBME wants a novel method with demonstrated significance; a null benchmark on 23+16 subjects in 8 pages is a poor fit. The Cheung paper is useful to cite (ED metric, leakage prevalence) and shows the editorial board accepts the leakage argument, but at review/meta-analysis scale. Rank low.

findings.title: IEEE TIM: screening explicitly rejects algorithm papers on existing datasets without measurement-performance or metrology framing
findings.summary: Authors page: regular papers minimum 5 pages, no maximum but overlength charges apply (IMS overlength agreement: free up to 8 pages, $265/$220 per page thereafter); short papers 3-4 pages. Papers 'typically rejected without peer review' if they: have the main novel contribution in another discipline with only some instrumentation content; 'Propose algorithms without showing they improve measurement performance'; 'Ignore established metrology guidance (GUM, VIM)'; 'treat algorithmic metrics as instrument performance'; 'Rely only on simulation or existing datasets, without I&M discussion or a strong justification for no experimental validation'. Topical guides exist for 'Medical/Biomedical and Healthcare' (10.1109/MIM.2016.7579063), 'Machine Learning: basics (measurement error and terminology)' (10.1109/MIM.2021.9400955) and 'AI ... uncertainty in measurement systems' (10.1109/OJIM.2025.3621742). Publication page: 'A large number of submissions are immediately rejected at first screening stage.' OpenAlex 2022-2026 PPG+glucose in TIM: only reviews (BP measurement review 2026, dehydration IoMT 2025), no PPG-glucose primary paper.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Two of the stated desk-reject criteria (existing public datasets only; algorithms not shown to improve measurement) describe this paper. Only viable if rewritten as a measurement-uncertainty study with GUM-style treatment, which it is not. Rank lowest.

findings.title: IEEE Sensors Journal: 8-page limit, $175/page overlength, device-centred scope but includes 'Sensor Data Processing'; published the Yoshizawa 2023 data-leakage paper on PPG/ECG BP
findings.source: https://ieee-sensors.org/ieee-sensors-journal/for-authors/ ; https://ieee-sensors.org/ieee-sensors-journal/ ; Yoshizawa, Yamamoto, Ohtsuki, IEEE Sensors J. 2023, DOI 10.1109/JSEN.2023.3272921
findings.summary: For-authors page: submissions 'should not exceed 8 pages formatted in double-columns', $175 per page beyond eight (12 for reviews), charges 'not negotiable or voluntary', graphical abstract required. Scope: 'theory, design, fabrication, manufacturing and applications of devices for sensing ... with emphasis on the electronics and physics aspect of sensors', topic list includes 'Sensor Data Processing (soft computing with sensor data, e.g., pattern recognition, machine learning ...)'. Precedent: 'Investigation of Data Leakage in Deep-Learning-Based Blood Pressure Estimation Using Photoplethysmogram/Electrocardiogram' (2023) shows segment- and record-level splits inflate accuracy vs subject-level split and that a 'record' in the cuffless-BP dataset is not a subject. OpenAlex 2022-2026 finds 11 PPG+glucose items, mostly hardware/system papers (186 uW glucose SoC 2022; dual-channel PPG + pulse-arrival velocity 2023; infrared pulse sensor + hybrid NN 2024; dual-wavelength transmission PPG 2025; wrist-worn CNN-SVR platform 2026; Sun & Kosmas domain-generalization 2025 DOI 10.1109/jsen.2025.3542385). Third-party sites cite ~40-45% acceptance (unverified).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: A leakage-critique precedent exists in exactly this journal, and PPG-glucose papers are routinely published there, but the paper contains no sensor/hardware contribution and both datasets are third-party. Fit moderate; 8 pages is tight for three contributions.

findings.title: IEEE OJEMB: gold OA (US$2160 APC 2026), Science/Technology templates, ~3000-word main text + 4000-word supplement, 14-page cap, fast pre-review; no negative-results policy; PPG-only patient-independent and comparative BP papers published
findings.summary: About page: scope 'the development and application of engineering concepts and methods to biology, medicine and health sciences'; APC US$2160 for 2026 (5% IEEE member / 20% society member discount); 'pre-review' decision within days. Manuscript-formats page: 'Science papers allow authors to focus primarily on their scientific discoveries (page limit: 14 pages); Technology papers put more emphasis on the development of a technology ... (page limit: 14 pages)'; 'Both formats are limited to about 3,000 words of text, but can be supplemented by a separate Supplementary Materials section' limited to 4,000 words and up to 10 display items. OpenAlex 2022-2026: 2 PPG/glucose-adjacent hits only; leakage-related hits include 'Continuous Patient-Independent Estimation of Respiratory Rate and Blood Pressure Using Robust Spectro-Temporal Features Derived From Photoplethysmogram Only' (2023) and 'Gyrosphygmogram-Based Blood Pressure Estimation: A Comparative Study of PTT and CNN-LSTM' (2026). No statement on negative results, replication or datasets.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Fast and OA, same EMBS reviewer pool as TBME/JBHI but lower bar; the 3,000-word main-text cap forces the artefact + benchmark into a Science-format short paper with the harness in supplement. Fit moderate; APC applies.

findings.title: Physiological Measurement: scope explicitly includes 'Benchmarking existing algorithms', 'rigorous large-scale validation of existing methods' and 'measurement standards and guidelines', but requires 30+ human subjects per group
findings.source: https://publishingsupport.iopscience.iop.org/?p=3614 ; https://www.ipem.ac.uk/publications/ipem-journals/physiological-measurement/ ; Süzen, Physiol. Meas. 47(11):115001 (2026) DOI 10.1088/1361-6579/aeb8de ; Charlton et al. 2023 roadmap DOI 10.1088/1361-6579/acead2 ; Koppula et al. 2022 DOI 10.1088/1361-6579/ac6d3f
findings.summary: IOP scope page: Methodological and Application tracks; application track lists 'Benchmarking existing algorithms'; scope stresses 'rigorous large-scale validation of existing methods' and 'Physiological measurement standards and guidelines'. Article types: Research papers 'not normally more than 8000 words' (structured abstract Objective/Approach/Main results/Significance), Letters <= 3000 words, Notes ('Brief descriptions of a single piece of apparatus or a technique') <= 3500 words, Comments <= 1800 words. Hard rule: 'For papers that report measurements on groups of human subjects we require the number of subjects in each group to be 30+. This is for both statistical reasons and for clinical credibility'; papers below threshold need prior contact with the journal. Adopts IOP standard data policy; IPEM page says the journal 'encourages publication of data and code as well as results'. No page limits, no negative-results statement. Published examples: Süzen 2026 (14 participants, fNIRS) on correction-stage information leakage distorting benchmark comparisons; Charlton & Allen 2023 wearable PPG roadmap (states 'processes for validating devices should be carefully designed'); Koppula 2022 PPG-based insulin-resistance tracking with 51 subjects (positive). OpenAlex 2022-2026: 12 PPG+glucose hits, none a PPG-glucose regression study.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Topically the best match in the whole list (benchmarking, validation of existing methods, standards, code/data encouraged, 8000 words). The 30+ subjects rule is the obstacle: Mendeley n=23 and BIG IDEAs n=16 both fall below it; the Süzen 2026 paper (n=14) shows exceptions are granted for methodology papers, so a pre-submission enquiry framing the paper as a methodological/benchmark study is required. The artefact report alone could go as a Note (<=3500 words).

findings.title: npj Digital Medicine: no length limit for Articles, Brief Communication 1000-1500 words, Matters Arising <=1200 words for 'challenges, clarifications, or ... replication of the published work'; the BIG IDEAs dataset's own paper (Bent et al. 2021) is in this journal
findings.source: https://www.nature.com/npjdigitalmed/content-types ; Bent et al., npj Digit. Med. 4:89 (2021) DOI 10.1038/s41746-021-00465-w (PMC8172541) ; Matters Arising example DOI 10.1038/s41746-019-0186-x
findings.summary: Content-types page: Article (abstract <=150 words, no stated main-text limit, ~60 refs), Brief Communication (1,000-1,500 words, ~20 refs), Matters Arising ('not to exceed 1,200 words', <=15 refs; 'may highlight challenges, clarifications, or in some cases, replication of the published work'), Comment 1,000-2,000, Perspective <=3,000, Review 3,000-4,000. No statement on negative results, reproducibility or benchmarks. Bent et al. 2021 (Duke BIG IDEAs Lab, 16 participants, ~25,000 paired CGM/smartwatch points, 10 days) reported 'up to 84% and 87% accuracy' for detecting personalised glucose deviations and predicting interstitial glucose. Prior Matters Arising on wearable ML (Ueno et al. 2019 on Green et al.) argued that including training patients in the confusion matrix 'might result in the over-estimate performance of the model'. OpenAlex 2022-2026: 95 wearable+glucose and 10 PPG+cuffless-BP items, mostly positive device/validation studies or reviews; 2025 'Integration of AI and wearable technology in diabetes' review; 2026 'Towards trustworthy AI-driven cuffless blood pressure monitoring'. Acceptance rate not published; IF ~15 (third-party, conflicting).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Full Article unlikely (engineering-heavy, non-diabetic cohorts, n=23/16, null). The realistic route is a Matters Arising on Bent et al. 2021 reporting that on the same cohort, under a chronological split with guard gap, no PPG model beats each subject's own mean; that confines the piece to 1,200 words and to the BIG IDEAs result only.

findings.title: SCOOP RISK 1: Ramesh et al., ISWC 2026 (ACM) re-evaluated five published PPG-glucose methods on VitalDB and MUST (= the Mendeley dataset) under random, participant-aware, LSPO and OOD splits; all collapse to the mean baseline; Clarke A+B hides failure; pipeline code released
findings.source: ACM ISWC 2026 pp. 127-133, DOI 10.1145/3830727.3834821 (published 2026-09-30) ; arXiv:2608.01820 (https://arxiv.org/html/2608.01820v1) ; code https://github.com/R-Supraja/bgl-evaluation-pipeline
findings.summary: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. Datasets: VitalDB (4,872 cases / 4,626 participants) and MUST (Kermani & Esmaeili 2023, 23 individuals, 67 sessions, i.e. the Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn recordings). Methods: ResNet-34 (Zeynali 2025), 1D-CNN (Alghlayini 2023), MFCC+XGBoost (Prabha 2022), features+PLS (Islam 2021), features+XGBoost (Gupta 2021). Results (MAE mg/dL; R2): global baseline 26.40/-0.00 random, 30.61/-0.10 participant-aware, 26.39/-0.00 LSPO; best model under random split 13.97/0.60 (Zeynali) falls to 25.93/-0.04 under LSPO; all models within ~1 mg/dL of baseline under LSPO; OOD (train VitalDB, test MUST) R2 -0.06 to -0.34. 'Over 90% of predictions fall within Clarke Error Grid zones A+B for every model and split, including the baseline.' No label artefact reported; BIG IDEAs not used; original works published no code.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Covers most of contribution (2) on the Mendeley recordings and the Clarke-grid argument, four months before any submission of ours. Our remaining novelty on Mendeley: the clean-dataset.csv artefact itself, recording-level aggregation, the 1D/2D-CWT/3D-Takens fusion ablation, and the demographic-ridge baseline. The draft must cite this paper and position itself as extending it; any venue's reviewers will find it.

findings.title: SCOOP RISK 2: Shen et al., NeurIPS 2026 workshop poster 'Data Leakage in PPG-based Non-invasive Blood Glucose Prediction' (three datasets, TinyML/CBHFF/CatBoost, RTTS vs subject-wise vs PAS vs LSPO vs OOD)
findings.source: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/162809 (Responsible Communication of Machine Learning Research in Biomedicine workshop)
findings.summary: Authors Junyi Shen, Hongmei Liu, Veronica Liesaputra, Yuan Zhang, Zhiyi Huang. Findings: random splitting gives the best scores, performance 'drops substantially under subject-separated and cross-dataset evaluation'; participant-aware splitting did not consistently beat LSPO; OOD gives 'near-zero or negative R2'; 'Clarke Error Grid results stayed high (97-100% of predictions in Zones A+B) even when regression performance was poor'. Dataset names not on the page; CBHFF is the JBHI 2024 Ali et al. model. No label artefact reported.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Second independent 2026 group making the leakage + Clarke-grid point. Strengthens the case that the field is now receptive, weakens any 'first to show' claim.

findings.title: SCOOP RISK 3: Seyedebrahimi, Ojeda, Zarrintaj, medRxiv Aug 2026: leakage-controlled fusion on BIG IDEAs (v1.1.2, 15 participants): wrist signals (PPG/EDA/temp/ACC) carry no glucose information beyond the cohort mean
findings.summary: Task: 30-min-ahead glucose forecasting from 2 h history; 5-fold subject-grouped CV with a split test (tests/test_splits.py); models: linear/ridge/lasso/elastic net, GBT, FCN, early-fusion TCN; baselines: CGM-history only, wristband only, time-of-day only, training mean. RMSE mg/dL: CGM-only linear 13.90 +/- 0.58; CGM + wrist summary 13.56 -> 13.60; TCN 14.66 -> 14.68; wristband only 22.58; time-of-day only 22.63; predict training mean 22.76. Conclusion: 'Sensor fusion cannot recover information the sensor does not acquire'; wrist-only models equal the time-of-day and mean baselines.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Covers the headline of our contribution (4) on the same PhysioNet cohort. Our protocol differs (within-subject chronological 70/30 split with 1-h guard gap, raw 64 Hz BVP windows into 1D/2D/3D networks, subject-own-mean null, per-reading metrics) and we use v1.1.3 with 16 subjects, but the conclusion is identical. Must be cited; the within-subject chronological protocol and guard-gap argument become the differentiator.

findings.title: The artefact derivative is identifiable: Kaggle 'PPG signal with Blood sugar level data' (uploader muhammadyasirsaleem) ships clean-dataset.csv (46.76 MB) with PPG_Signal / Glucose_Level / Age columns; no published paper reports its label-replication pattern
findings.summary: Kaggle listing describes a PPG_Signal column of raw PPG values and a Glucose_Level column plus Age; the companion GitHub repo (linear/decision-tree/polynomial regression, no split method stated) links only to Kaggle, not Mendeley. The original Mendeley dataset is 'The dataset of photoplethysmography signals collected from a pulse sensor to measure blood glucose level', contributors Ali Kermani and Hossein Esmaeili, University of Science and Technology of Mazandaran, 67 raw PPG signals from 23 individuals, 2175 Hz, published 26 June 2023, CC BY 4.0 (also on IEEE DataPort DOI 10.21227/mekr-0a81). None of Ramesh 2026, Shen 2026, the QUMPHY D4 benchmark report (arXiv 2604.01398) or the searched literature reports a label-cycling artefact in any PPG-glucose derivative.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Contribution (1) appears to be genuinely unreported and is the paper's strongest unique claim; the draft should name the Kaggle derivative explicitly and show which published pipelines use the same column layout. Separately, ieee_paper.tex bibitem 'ppgdataset2023' credits 'D. Kumar, V. Kumar, and S. Chaudhary' for the Mendeley dataset; Mendeley lists Kermani & Esmaeili. That must be corrected before submission anywhere.

findings.title: Sister-field precedents: PPG-BP negative/pitfall papers have been published in Scientific Reports, Scientific Data, Machine Learning: Health and IEEE TBME, establishing the genre
findings.source: Mehta et al., Sci. Rep. 2024 DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-68862-1 ; Fritzsche & Senner, Sci. Rep. 16 (2026) DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-66882-7 ; Gonzalez et al., Sci. Data 2023 DOI 10.1038/s41597-023-02020-6 ; Moulaeifard, Charlton, Strodthoff, Mach. Learn.: Health 1:010501 (2025) DOI 10.1088/3049-477X/ae01a8
findings.summary: Mehta 2024: 'many papers fall prey to data leakage and unrealistic constraints on the task and preprocessing steps'. Fritzsche 2026: 'using our dataset and the subject-wise data split in our training pipeline, we were unable to reproduce the reported high correlations and low MAEs'; dataset integrity and calibration matter more than architecture. Gonzalez 2023 benchmark: in leaky splits 94.6-100% of test samples share a subject with training. Moulaeifard 2025 (IOP's new ML:Health journal, sister to Physiological Measurement): external-dataset MAE 10.0-18.6 mmHg SBP without calibration, in-distribution results 'an overly optimistic measure'.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Shows the realistic homes for this genre are Nature Portfolio's Scientific Reports/Scientific Data and IOP's Physiological Measurement / Machine Learning: Health, plus IEEE Access and Sensors J; the flagship IEEE transactions take it only as large reviews (Cheung 2024 TBME).

findings.title: IEEE Data Descriptions (new IEEE OA journal) accepts 4-8 page dataset 'descriptor' articles with data-quality assessment but descriptors 'cannot claim new scientific findings or experimental results'
findings.summary: Three article types (descriptors, collections, metadata); recommended length 4-8 pages; open review; target publication < 10 weeks; aim includes 'data quality assessments'.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: A possible outlet for the artefact characterisation + integrity test alone (a quality assessment of a public derivative), if the benchmark goes elsewhere; not suitable for the null-result benchmark.

implications: Frank answer to the 'ground-breaking / easily publishable in an IEEE Transactions' question: no. Between June and October 2026 three independent groups (Ramesh et al. ISWC 2026 on the same Mendeley/MUST recordings; Shen et al. NeurIPS 2026 workshop; Seyedebrahimi et al. medRxiv on the same BIG IDEAs cohort) published the leakage + mean-baseline + Clarke-grid conclusion. The paper is now a confirmatory benchmark with one unique element: the clean-dataset.csv label-replication artefact and the integrity test that detects it.
