Ranking of fit for the paper as currently constituted (artefact + null benchmark on 23+16 subjects + code): 1) IEEE Access (scope names negative results; Costa 2023 precedent; no n threshold; ~20% acceptance). 2) IEEE JBHI (topical home of the claims refuted, 14 pages, accepts n=21 PPG-glucose work; 14.9% acceptance; needs the harness framed as reusable). 3) Physiological Measurement (best written scope fit: benchmarking, validation, standards, 8000 words, code encouraged; blocked by the 30+ subjects rule unless the editor pre-approves a methodology framing). 4) IEEE Sensors Journal (Yoshizawa 2023 precedent; but no sensor contribution; 8 pages). 5) IEEE OJEMB (fast, OA, 3000-word cap, US$2160 APC). 6) npj Digital Medicine (only as a <=1200-word Matters Arising on Bent et al. 2021, BIG IDEAs part only). 7) IEEE TBME (novel-method mandate, 8 pages, ~19% acceptance). 8) IEEE TIM (desk-reject criteria explicitly cover existing-dataset algorithm papers without measurement-performance claims).

To be competitive at JBHI or Physiological Measurement rather than Access, the paper should be refactored around what the three 2026 papers do not have: (a) the artefact and a general detector for one-to-many join flattening in biosignal tables; (b) recording-level and reading-level (not window-level) metrics with the null model's Clarke zone A alongside; (c) the within-subject chronological protocol with guard gap on BIG IDEAs, contrasted with Seyedebrahimi's 5-fold subject-grouped forecasting; (d) the 1D vs CWT vs Takens vs fusion ablation under LOSO; (e) re-running Ramesh et al.'s released pipeline on the Kaggle derivative to show the artefact inflates even their protocol (direct, citable link).

Mandatory edits before any submission: cite Ramesh 2026 (ACM DOI 10.1145/3830727.3834821), Shen 2026, Seyedebrahimi 2026, Cheung 2024 (TBME, 'explained deviation'), Costa 2023 (IEEE Access), Yoshizawa 2023 (Sensors J); fix the Mendeley dataset attribution (Kermani & Esmaeili, Univ. of Science and Technology of Mazandaran, not 'Kumar et al.'); name the Kaggle derivative explicitly; drop any 'first to show' wording about leakage or the Clarke grid.

Length planning by venue: Access/Sensors J/TBME 8 pages (Access has no hard cap but 8 is customary), JBHI 14 incl. supplement with mandatory charges above 8, OJEMB ~3000 words + 4000-word supplement, Physiol Meas <=8000 words (Note <=3500), npj DM Matters Arising <=1200 words. The current draft (two cohorts, two tables, four figures, five recommendations) is sized for JBHI or Physiological Measurement, not for an 8-page journal.

If the user wants an IEEE Transactions specifically, JBHI is the only realistic one and only with the refactor above; TBME and TIM should not be attempted with this content. If speed and certainty matter more than prestige, IEEE Access or OJEMB; if scope fit matters most, write to the Physiological Measurement editor before submitting, citing the 30+ rule and the Süzen 2026 (n=14) methodology precedent.
gaps_or_uncertainties: Could not fetch the official OJEMB 'formats and instructions' page or the embs.org TBME aims-and-scope page directly (404/redirects); OJEMB limits (14 pages, ~3000 words + 4000-word supplement) and TBME limits (8/3/4/10 pages) come from search-engine extracts of those pages and should be re-checked on embs.org before submission.

IEEE Access acceptance rate is stated as 20% on ieeeaccess.ieee.org/authors but third-party sites quote 27% and 40-50%; TBME 18.7% is from a 2018 EiC message; JBHI 14.9% is from the embs.org statistics page of uncertain date; no acceptance rate found for Physiological Measurement, npj Digital Medicine, OJEMB, TIM or Sensors J (one blog says 40-45% for Sensors J, unverified).

medRxiv and dl.acm.org blocked direct fetches (403); Seyedebrahimi et al. details come from the GitHub README and search extracts, and the ISWC venue/pages come from OpenAlex metadata rather than the ACM page.
Shen et al. NeurIPS 2026 page does not name its three datasets; whether MUST/Mendeley or BIG IDEAs is among them is unknown.

No published source reports the clean-dataset.csv label-cycling artefact; absence was checked by search only (Kaggle page text could not be fetched), so a reviewer may still surface a Kaggle discussion thread or blog noting it.

Physiological Measurement's 30+ subjects rule is quoted from the IOP publishing-support page; how often exceptions are granted for methodology/benchmark papers is not documented (Süzen 2026 with 14 participants is one observed case).

npj Digital Medicine's content-types page gives no main-text limit for Articles and no stated policy on negative results; whether the editors would consider a Matters Arising on a 2021 paper five years later is untested.
Nothing on 'typical length' was found for IEEE Access beyond custom; IEEE Access imposes APC and has no formal page cap on its author page.

sweep:prior-work.angle: PRIOR WORK: peer-reviewed / preprint papers (2018-2026) estimating blood glucose from PPG (alone or + simple signals) with ML/DL; dataset, split protocol, reported errors, null-baseline reporting; flags for the Kaggle clean-dataset.csv and the Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn dataset.

findings.title: DATASET PROVENANCE (not a paper): Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn is by Kermani & Esmaeili, not 'Kumar'; the Kaggle CSV is literally named clean-dataset.csv
findings.summary: Mendeley page: contributors Ali Kermani and Hossein Esmaeili, University of Science and Technology of Mazandaran, Behshahr, Iran. 23 individuals, 67 raw PPG signals, 2175 Hz, 550 nm green LED + APDS-9008 photodiode, Atmega328 12-bit ADC, index finger, Accu-Chek Active reference. Labels folder has 68 .mat/.csv vs 67 signals (unexplained). Versions: v1 (cited as .1 by Zeynali), v2 (cited by Soliman 2024), v3 (Jul 2023), v4 (Sep 2025, no version notes). The dataset's companion paper (Kermani & Esmaeili, BioImpacts 2025, doi:10.34172/bi.30589) states glucose range 70-185 mg/dL, ages 20-61, 15 M / 8 F. Kaggle: dataset 'PPG signal with Blood sugar level data' by muhammadyasirsaleem; main file is clean-dataset.csv (46.76 MB); columns per the companion GitHub README: PPG Signal (mV), Heart Rate (bpm), Systolic Peak (mmHg), Diastolic Peak (mmHg), Pulse Area, Gender, Height, Weight, Age Range, plus Glucose_Level target and Patient_Id. No Mendeley DOI or provenance is given on Kaggle/GitHub. No peer-reviewed paper was found that cites this Kaggle CSV; only the uploader's own notebook/repo (polynomial regression, no numbers in text).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The draft's \bibitem{ppgdataset2023} ('D. Kumar, V. Kumar, S. Chaudhary') is wrong: the dataset authors are Kermani & Esmaeili; cite the Mendeley version actually loaded (v1/.1 ... v4/.4) and the BioImpacts 2025 paper. The sentence 'judging by its column layout, for other published models' is unsupported by the literature search: name the Kaggle dataset/file explicitly and state that no published model using it was found. Kaggle total row count (844,946) could not be verified online (page shows only bin counts); 67 x 21,900 = 1,467,300 raw samples, so the CSV is a subset; verify the mapping locally.

findings.title: Reassessing the Feasibility of PPG-Based Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Level Estimation (Ramesh, Neufeld, Kuttner, Roddiger, Beigl; KIT)
findings.summary: Re-implements five published PPG->glucose methods (Zeynali 2025 ResNet-34; Alghlayini 2023 1D-CNN; Prabha 2022 MFCC+XGBoost; Islam 2021 features+PLS; Gupta 2021 features+XGBoost) on VitalDB (4,626 surgical patients, 4,872 cases, 500 Hz, glucose 44-525 mg/dL) under three splits (random window 80/20; participant-aware; leave-some-participants-out 5-fold) and OOD test on the Mendeley 'MUST' set (23 subj, 67 sessions, 88-183 mg/dL). Includes an explicit train-mean baseline. LSPO results: mean baseline MAE 26.39, R2 -0.00, MARD 22.5%, zone A 52.3%, A+B 97.4%; ResNet-34 MAE 25.93, R2 -0.04, zone A 55.6%; 1D-CNN MAE 26.05; XGBoost MAE 25.4-25.8, R2 <=0.05. Random split inflates ResNet-34 to MAE 13.97 / R2 0.60 / zone A 82%. OOD on MUST: mean baseline MAE 16.00, MARD 14.1%, zone A 77.6%, A+B 100%; models MAE 13.4-18.2, R2 -0.06 to -0.34. RMSE not reported. Conclusion: random splits leak; zone A+B >90% for every model including the mean; R2 ~0 subject-wise. Notes that sub-windows inherit one label per event but does not identify a label-cycling artefact.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Closest prior to our thesis and must be cited and differentiated. Their MUST mean-baseline (MAE 16.0, zone A 77.6%) is a direct external reference for our train-mean row on the same raw recordings. What they do not have: LOSO on the raw Mendeley recordings themselves, the clean-dataset.csv label-replication artefact, a within-subject chronological protocol with guard gap on wearable BVP vs CGM, and the multi-view (1D/2D/3D) fusion ablation. Novelty must be framed around those four items, not around 'random splits leak'.

findings.title: Non-invasive blood glucose monitoring using PPG signals with various deep learning models and implementation using TinyML (Zeynali, Alipour, Tarvirdizadeh, Ghamari)
findings.summary: FLAG: uses Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn/1 ('MUST') as external test set. Train/val/test on VitalDB: 6,388 subjects, 35,358 BGL records, 699,072 10-s segments (each BGL treated as constant over +/-8 min), 70/15/15 split 'of the segments' (random segment-level; subject-wise not stated). Models ResNet34-1D (7.4M params), VGG16, CNN-LSTM-attention. VitalDB test, 1-s ResNet34: RMSE 27.48, MAE 18.54, MARD 15.5%, R2 0.40, zone A 72.6%, D 1.4%; VGG16 and CNN-LSTM R2 negative. MUST test, ResNet34: RMSE 19.7, MAE 14.8, MARD 12.8%, zone A 76.6%, B 23.4% (abstract headline). No null/mean baseline. Paper variously says 67 signals / 23 subjects / '67 testing subjects'.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Its MUST zone A (76.6%) is below the train-mean zone A (77.6%) that Ramesh et al. measure on the same set, illustrating our 'zone A without a null is uninformative' point. Random segment-level split on VitalDB with +/-8 min label windows is exactly the leakage pattern we warn about. Cite as an example that reports no baseline.

findings.title: Non-Invasive Glucose Level Monitoring from PPG using a Hybrid CNN-GRU Deep Learning Network (Soliman, Nor, Fratu, Halunga, Omer, Mubark)
findings.summary: FLAG: Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn/2 ('Mazandaran v2'): 23 subjects, 67 signals, glucose 88-187 mg/dL (text inconsistent: 98-138). Gaussian-noise augmentation 67 -> 269 samples, then data 'shuffled' and split train/val/test (ratios and grouping not stated) plus 10-fold CV (grouping unit not stated). Test: MAE 2.96, RMSE 3.94, R2 0.97, MAPE 2.40%, Clarke zone A 100%. Per-fold MAE 0.77-3.82. No null baseline. Augmented copies may straddle splits.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The '<5 mg/dL on 67 recordings' number is the kind of result our LOSO shows is unattainable without leakage (augmented duplicates + shuffled split). Good motivating citation next to our train-mean MAE on the same recordings.

findings.title: Hybrid deep learning-based blood glucose level monitoring using PPG signals (Soliman, Nor, Omer, Mubarak)
findings.source: Signal, Image and Video Processing 20(6):313 (2026), doi:10.1007/s11760-026-05368-5
findings.summary: FLAG: uses the 'publicly available Mazandaran dataset' (Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn). Bi-LSTM + two CNNs. Reported MAE 13.8 mg/dL, RMSE 16.84 mg/dL (from search abstracts). Split protocol and null baseline not retrievable (paywalled; Crossref has no abstract).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Same group as the CNN-GRU preprint, now reporting ~5x larger error on the same data; worth citing as evidence that the headline numbers on this dataset are protocol-dependent. Split unknown: mark as such.

findings.title: Interpretable non-invasive glucose monitoring: an attention-based deep learning framework for visualizing hemodynamic correlates in PPG signals (Syamsul, Kim)
findings.source: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology 14:1843361 (3 Jul 2026), doi:10.3389/fbioe.2026.1843361, PMC13375809
findings.summary: FLAG: Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn/3. 23 adults; 348 PPG segments (windowing described inconsistently: 1000 Hz / 10,000-sample vs 40 s at 250 Hz). Split described three ways: subject-wise 16/3/4 train/val/test; 'LOSO'; and 'did not perform a dedicated subject-independent evaluation' (Sec. 7.5). AG-CRNN (1D-CNN + GRU + temporal attention + demographics): MAE 11.59, RMSE 15.40, Pearson r 0.83. No MARD, R2 or Clarke. Baselines: RNN/LSTM/GRU/1D-CNN only; no null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Directly comparable cohort; its r=0.83 would be far above our LOSO 1-D CNN r, but its own text contradicts whether evaluation is subject-independent. Cite with that caveat; it also uses demographics as input, which our ridge-demographics baseline shows carry little signal.

findings.title: Photoplethysmography based non-invasive blood glucose estimation using systolic-diastolic framing MFCC features and machine learning regression (Kermani, Esmaeili) - the dataset creators' own paper
findings.summary: FLAG: Mendeley 37pm7jk7jn/3 (own data): 67 signals, 23 volunteers, glucose 70-185 mg/dL. SDFMFCC features + SVR (also RF, AdaBoost, GB). Reported RMSE 26.01 mg/dL, MAE 4.014 mg/dL, 'MARD 0.195%', 'accuracy 99.8%', Clarke zone A 99.273% (internally inconsistent: RMSE 26 with MAE 4 and MARD 0.2%). Train/test split or CV not stated anywhere in the text. No null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Authoritative source for cohort facts (range, sex split, sensor). Its reported numbers are mutually inconsistent and unprotocolled; cite it for the data description, not for accuracy comparison. Note our LOSO train-mean MAE on the same recordings for contrast.

findings.title: 90% Accuracy for Photoplethysmography-Based Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Prediction by Deep Learning with Cohort Arrangement and Quarterly Measured HbA1c (Chu, Yang, Lu, Chang, Hsieh, Yang)
findings.summary: 2,538 Taiwanese subjects (1,682 medicated, 856 not), two 1-min PPG segments each (averaged to 250-pt pulse) + 17 handcrafted features (+HbA1c). Random 9:1 split repeated 10x, subject-wise not stated (overlap possible). 1D-CNN micro/macro blocks. All-subjects, no HbA1c: zone A 60.6%, RMSE 36.7, MAE 25.4, MAPE 19%, R2 0.06. No-medication + HbA1c: zone A 94.2%, RMSE 12.4, MAE 8.9, R2 0.71. Medication, no HbA1c: R2 -0.09. No null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Largest PPG-glucose cohort; shows R2 near/below zero for PPG alone at scale, with 'accuracy' driven by HbA1c and cohort selection. Good citation for 'zone A 60% at n=2538' versus small-cohort claims.

findings.title: Deduction learning for precise noninvasive measurements of blood glucose with a dozen rounds of data for model training (Lu, Yang, Chu, Hsieh, Yang)
findings.summary: 30 diabetic volunteers, 6-15 fasting rounds each (two 1-min PPG per round, Accu-Chek Mobile reference), TI AFE4490. Personalised chronological split: train rounds 1-12, test rounds 13-15. DL+screening: MAE 12.07, RMSE 13.93, zone A 100%; plain deduction learning MAE 25.96, zone A 80%; single-channel CNN (induction) MAE 38.38, zone A 55%; RF 37-40. No MARD; no null/mean baseline. Wilcoxon p=0.063.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: One of few chronological within-subject protocols; it needs a paired 'pretest' reference reading, i.e. calibration, and the non-calibrated CNN gives MAE 38. Supports our point that un-calibrated PPG does not track glucose within subject.

findings.title: Improving non-invasive glucose estimation with monthly calibrated photoplethysmography and implicit HbA1c (Chu, Hsieh, Chang, Liaw, Yang)
findings.summary: Three Taiwanese diabetic cohorts: 17/10/20 participants, 65/67/167 records, fasting 60-s PPG + finger-prick. Subject-wise leave-one-out CV for cohorts 1-2; cohort 3 tested on models trained on 1-2. Dual-channel 'deduction learning' with one monthly pretest. MARD 9.59/12.23/16.40%; Clarke zone A 98.7/87.9/78.3% (0-30 day); Parkes A 98.7/92.4/90.4%. Baseline (no-pretest NN) Parkes A 86.2/69.9/65.2%. MAE/RMSE only in supplement. No null/mean baseline. Heavy exclusions (e.g. 70/182 pairs).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Shows that the only subject-wise results near clinical accuracy rely on a per-user recent calibration reading. Cite in Discussion: PPG-alone cross-subject estimation is not what this literature actually delivers.

findings.title: Multi-View Cross-Fusion Transformer Based on Kinetic Features for Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Measurement Using PPG Signal (Chen, Qin, Ma, Wei, Zhang, Zhang, Jovanov)
findings.summary: Clinical dataset of 260 subjects; subject-wise 5-fold CV. MvCFT fuses raw PPG waveform view with kinetic-feature view via cross-attention transformer. RMSE 1.129 mmol/L (~20.3 mg/dL), MAE 0.659 mmol/L (~11.9 mg/dL), Clarke zone A 87.89%. A later 2,510-subject validation reportedly 81.39% (search snippet). Null baseline: unknown (full text paywalled; not in abstract).
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Closest architectural prior to our multi-view fusion (IEEE JBHI, subject-wise). Must be cited in Related Work; note its zone A of 87.9% is reported without a mean-predictor reference. Our result that fusion adds nothing at n=23 should be positioned against this n=260 result (sample size, not architecture, may be the difference).

findings.title: PPG Based Noninvasive Blood Glucose Monitoring Using Multi-View Attention and Cascaded BiLSTM Hierarchical Feature Fusion Approach (Ali, Li, Fan, Nie)
findings.summary: 21 participants, up to 6 days of PPG + BG each. Convolutional multi-view attention + cascaded BiLSTM + bilinear-pooling fusion. RMSE 1.67 mmol/L (~30 mg/dL), MARD 17.88%, Clarke A+B 98.80% (zone A alone not in abstract). Split protocol not in abstract (paywalled). No null baseline mentioned.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Second direct 'multi-view attention' prior in an IEEE Transactions-level venue; its MARD of 17.9% on 21 subjects is in the same range as a subject-mean null on free-living CGM data. Cite and note that zone A+B alone is reported.

findings.title: A Deep Learning Model That Combines ResNet and Transformer Architectures for Real-Time Blood Glucose Measurement Using PPG Signals (Chen, Wang, Hong, Wu)
findings.summary: MIMIC-III waveform (125 Hz, 10-s windows) with ICU glucose labels; ~9,018 subjects / 370k signals (counts inconsistent across sections). 'Personalised' = sample-level 20% hold-out from same subjects; 'non-personalised' = held-out subjects. ResNet alone: MARD 9.25% personalised vs 19.17% non-personalised; zone A 91.0% vs 44.3%. ResNet+Transformer: MARD 11.69% vs 15.16%; zone A 82.7% vs 75.4%. 180-class soft-label classification 70-250 mg/dL. No MAE/RMSE; no null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Clean demonstration of the personalised-vs-held-out-subject gap (zone A 91% -> 44% for the same ResNet). Citable evidence that within-subject sample splits inflate accuracy.

findings.title: Engineering digital biomarkers of interstitial glucose from noninvasive smartwatches (Bent, Cho, Henriquez, Wittmann, Thacker, Feinglos, Crowley, Dunn) - the BIG IDEAs source paper
findings.source: npj Digital Medicine 4:89 (2021), doi:10.1038/s41746-021-00465-w, PMC8172541; dataset doi:10.13026/aw6y-fc44 (PhysioNet v1.1.3)
findings.summary: 16 participants (HbA1c 5.2-6.4), Dexcom G6 every 5 min (>25,000 readings), Empatica E4 (PPG-derived HR/HRV, EDA, TEMP, ACC) + food logs; 69 rolling features (5 min-24 h history, incl. diet and participant ID), XGBoost. Population model: leave-one-person-out CV, RMSE 21.22 +/- 4.14, MAPE 14.33%. Personalised: first contiguous 50% train / last 50% test (no guard gap), RMSE 21.10, MAPE 13.26% ('87% accuracy' = 100-MAPE). States models 'beat mean and median naive baselines' but gives no baseline numbers. No MAE, MARD or Clarke.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The reference result on our BIG IDEAs cohort. We should report RMSE and MAPE (and 100-MAPE) so our subject-mean null is comparable to their 21.2/14.3%; our contribution is the explicit null numbers and the 1-h guard gap they lack. Note their features include food logs and 24-h history, i.e. not PPG-only.

findings.title: Enhancing Wearable based Real-Time Glucose Monitoring via Phasic Image Representation Learning based Deep Learning (Zhu, Aimandi, Alam)
findings.summary: BIG IDEAs PhysioNet data: 16 participants, 8-10 days, E4 BVP + EDA + TEMP vs Dexcom G6. Modified frequency-domain recurrence plots -> ResNet-18. 70:30 train/validation split, nature (random / subject / chronological) not stated. RMSE 18.17, MAPE 12.35%, 'accuracy' 87.65% vs Bent's 21.22/85.67% (Duke numbers copied, not re-run). No MAE, Clarke, or null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Only other DL paper on BIG IDEAs BVP found; unspecified 70:30 split makes its 'improvement' over Bent uninterpretable. Cite as the example of why guard gaps and split declaration matter on CGM-aligned windows.

findings.title: An In-Ear PPG-Based Blood Glucose Monitor: A Proof-of-Concept Study (Hammour, Mandic)
findings.summary: 4 subjects (1 non-diabetic, 1 pre-diabetic, 1 T1D, 1 T2D), 244 two-minute in-ear 880 nm PPG recordings with Accu-Chek Performa reference over 9 recording days. Per-subject chronological split (first 7 days train with 5-fold CV, last 2 days test), ensemble regression trees. Test RMSE 17.5/17.8/25.3/42.8 mg/dL; MARD 12.8/13.3/18.4/13.5%; Clarke zone A 89.5/83.3/77.8/77.8% (avg ~82%), A+B 100%; r 0.54-0.68. No MAE; no null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: A properly chronological per-subject protocol (same spirit as our BIG IDEAs split) that still omits the subject-mean null; r of 0.5-0.7 on 4 subjects is the best within-subject correlation found in this search.

findings.title: A Noninvasive Glucose Monitoring SoC Based on Single Wavelength Photoplethysmography / A 186 uW PPG-Based Noninvasive Glucose Sensing SoC (Hina, Saadeh)
findings.summary: Single-wavelength NIR PPG, 10 handcrafted features, customised NMG-SVR on chip. 200 subjects. TBioCAS: R2 0.937, mARD 7.62%, RMSE 11.20; JSEN: mARD 6.9%, RMSE 10.20, R2 0.955 (per Hina & Saadeh 2022 Sensors review table, PMC9229484, which also lists zone A 95% for the 2020 paper). Split protocol (per-sample vs subject-wise) not stated in any abstract or the review; full texts paywalled. No null baseline reported.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The IEEE-venue results most often cited for '<10% MARD from PPG alone'; validation protocol is undocumented in accessible sources. Cite with 'split not reported'. Note the draft's \bibitem{hina2021noninvasive} is actually the 2022 Sensors review (22(13):4855), doi:10.3390/s22134855.

findings.title: Intelligent estimation of blood glucose level using wristband PPG signal and physiological parameters (Prabha, Yadav, Rani, Singh)
findings.source: Biomedical Signal Processing and Control 78:103876 (2022), doi:10.1016/j.bspc.2022.103876
findings.summary: 217 participants from a hospital in Cuenca, Ecuador (Empatica E4 wrist PPG at 64 Hz, ~2.5-4 min, lab Cobas 6000 / Accu-Chek reference; dataset from 'Database Proposal for Correlation of Glucose and PPG Signals', ICAETT 2019, restricted access). MFCC features + physiological parameters, SVR and XGBoost. SEP 9.78 mg/dL, 5.53 mg/dL after selecting 5 features, r = 0.99; Clarke/Bland-Altman 'clinically acceptable'. Split protocol not retrievable (paywalled). No null baseline. Re-implemented by Ramesh et al. 2026: R2 0.16 random, -0.03 participant-aware, 0.05 LSPO on VitalDB.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Example of r=0.99 on wristband PPG that collapses to R2~0 under subject-wise evaluation in an independent re-implementation. Also the 217-subject E4 dataset is a candidate for a third cohort if access can be obtained.

findings.title: Blood Glucose Level Estimation Using PPG Signals with Explainable AI Techniques (Adiguzel, Senturk, Polat)
findings.summary: Same 217-participant Cuenca E4 dataset (127 F / 90 M). Beat-segmented and averaged PPG, 51 features, CatBoost/XGBoost/ExtraTrees + SHAP. CatBoost: R2 0.71, MAE 25.21 mg/dL. Split not stated. No null baseline. (Not the Kaggle CSV: columns and n do not match.)
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Same data as Prabha 2022 but MAE 25 vs SEP 5.5: another instance of protocol-driven spread on one dataset. Low-tier venue; cite only if making the 'same dataset, 5x error spread' point.

findings.title: Blood Glucose Level Regression for Smartphone PPG Signals Using Machine Learning (Islam, Ahmed, Hassanuzzaman, Amir, Rahman)
findings.summary: Smartphone fingertip video (red channel) -> PPG; >=3 trials per subject, 191 trials total (subject count not retrieved; full text 403). Feature extraction + PLS/other regressors; best PLS SEP 17.02 mg/dL on an 'unbiased' dataset. No null baseline. Re-implemented by Ramesh 2026: R2 0.01 random / -0.05 participant-aware.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Representative handcrafted-feature baseline paper; cite for the 15-25 mg/dL feature-regression range claimed in our Related Work (currently attributed to the wrong reference).

findings.title: Towards non-invasive blood glucose measurement using machine learning: An all-purpose PPG system design (Sen Gupta, Kwon, Hossain, Kim)
findings.source: Biomedical Signal Processing and Control 68:102706 (2021), doi:10.1016/j.bspc.2021.102706
findings.summary: Three-wavelength (green/red/IR) fingertip prototype; handcrafted features; XGBoost. Hina & Saadeh review lists R2 0.88; n subjects and split not retrievable (paywalled, no abstract in Crossref/S2). Re-implemented by Ramesh 2026: R2 0.27 random, -0.00 participant-aware, 0.04 LSPO. Null baseline: not reported.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Another feature+GBDT paper whose accuracy vanishes subject-wise in independent re-evaluation; cite via Ramesh.

findings.title: Non invasive blood glucose estimation using green light photoplethysmography and machine learning (Khan, Malik, Khan, Abbasi, Arvanitis)
findings.source: Frontiers in Digital Health 8:1705086 (17 Feb 2026), doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1705086
findings.summary: 80 subjects, 160 recordings (fasting + post-glucose), SEN-11574 green pulse sensor on Arduino, ~127 Hz, 15 s; glucose 65-160 mg/dL. Random 50/50 train/test at record level (two records per subject -> subject overlap possible), no CV. Random forest: R2 0.92, MAE 4.8, RMSE 6.1 mg/dL. No MARD, no Clarke (future work), no null baseline. Predictions biased low in every range.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Same sensor class as the Mendeley pulse sensor; record-level random split with two records per subject is the exact leakage we describe. Useful 2026 example of MAE<5 claims without subject-wise evaluation.

findings.title: Non-invasive Blood Glucose Estimation from Wearable Physiological Signals (Zhang, Li, Wang, Yang, Lei)
findings.summary: New longitudinal benchmark: 183 participants, 285 days, wearable PPG + capillary glucose + cuff BP (to be released). Dynamic incremental learning with replay clustering. 5-fold subject-independent CV: MAE 0.64 +/- 0.01 mmol/L (~11.5 mg/dL), RMSE 1.29 +/- 0.10 mmol/L (~23 mg/dL), Clarke A+B 97.69%. Zone A alone, MARD, and null baseline not in abstract.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Largest subject-independent wearable-PPG result found; needs few reference labels per user (semi-calibrated). Watch for the dataset release as a possible third cohort; cite as current state of the art for subject-independent MAE.

findings.title: An Exploratory Study of Blood Glucose Estimation from Photoplethysmography Signals using Machine Learning (Bhatia, Ekbote; IIIT Delhi)
findings.summary: 5 volunteers, Empatica EmbracePlus PPG 64 Hz + FreeStyle Libre CGM (15-min) for 14 days. MLP. Within-subject temporal 80/20: MAPE 7.7-14.3% per day. Cross-subject (train 3, fine-tune 4th): MAE 1.06, RMSE 3.56 (units mmol/L implied), Lin's CCC 0.014, Clarke zone A 73.6%, zone E 25.6%. No null baseline; authors say results unstable and not for clinical use.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Independent wearable-PPG-vs-CGM study reaching the same negative within/cross-subject conclusion (CCC ~0). Small, but it is a released paired PPG/CGM dataset.

findings.title: A Deep Sparse Capsule Network for Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Level Estimation Using a PPG Sensor (Chellamani et al.)
findings.summary: Own data, 835 subjects at King Fahad Specialist Hospital (Tabuk), two 1-min PPG segments each (1700 samples at 115.2 Hz, i.e. ~15 s), invasive reference in mmol/L. 80:20 split 'of the 1700 samples' (per-sample; subject-wise not stated). DSCNet +/- self-attention. Reported MAPE 3.02, MAE 0.05, RMSE 0.062 (units unstated, likely normalised), MARD 10.81%, R2 0.98. No Clarke; no null baseline; multiple internal inconsistencies.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Example of a large-n paper with unreported units and per-sample split; cite cautiously or omit.

findings.title: A Noninvasive Blood Glucose Monitoring System Based on Smartphone PPG Signal Processing and Machine Learning (Zhang, Mei, Zhang, Ma, Lo, Chen, Zhang)
findings.source: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics 16(11):7209-7218 (2020), doi:10.1109/TII.2020.2975222
findings.summary: 80 subjects, smartphone camera PPG, Gaussian-fit features; 3-class classification (normal/borderline/warning), overall accuracy 81.49%; signal-validity classifier 97.54%. No regression metrics, split protocol not in abstract, no null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: IEEE Transactions precedent, but classification not regression; cite only as a smartphone-PPG example.

findings.title: Photoplethysmography Based Blood Glucose Estimation Using Convolutional Neural Networks (Alghlayini, Hosni, Atef)
findings.summary: Own prototype (PPG sensor + Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense); PPG-only CNN 89.28% Clarke zone A, 92.85% with mean-power-spectrum feature. n subjects, split, MAE/RMSE not in abstract. No null baseline. Re-implemented by Ramesh 2026: R2 0.00 under all splits.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Zone-A-only reporting with no error metric; useful as the archetype for 'zone A without a null'.

findings.title: Non-invasive estimate of blood glucose and blood pressure from a photoplethysmograph by means of machine learning techniques (Monte-Moreno) - pre-2018 foundational
findings.summary: 410 individuals, no personal calibration, cross-validation (type not specified in abstract). Random forest best: R2 0.90 for glucose; Clarke zone A 87.7%, B 10.3%, D 1.9%. No null baseline.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: The most-cited origin of the 'PPG predicts glucose' claim; outside the 2018-2026 window but should anchor the Related Work timeline.

findings.title: Selection of Noninvasive Features in Wrist-Based Wearable Sensors to Predict Blood Glucose Concentrations Using Machine Learning Algorithms (Bogue-Jimenez, Huang, Powell, Doblas)
findings.summary: OhioT1DM (6 subjects, HR/GSR/temp only, no raw PPG; 12-13k samples for 2 subjects analysed) and own 2-subject E4 dataset (~80 samples each, 14 features incl. BVP/IBI/HR). Random 75/25 per subject + 10-fold CV, per-subject models. Ohio: RMSE 66.3/46.4, R2 0.11/0.16, zone A 37.9/49.9%. UofM: RMSE 8.0/11.4, R2 0.78/0.70, zone A 100/94.4%. No MAE/MARD. No explicit mean baseline, but authors note Ohio predictions cluster near the mean and R2~0 'is no better than random'. Does not use BIG IDEAs.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Shows that random within-subject splits on T1D data still give zone A <50% once glucose actually varies, i.e. zone A is cohort-dependent (our Clarke argument). Not a PPG-alone paper.

findings.title: Noninvasive Hypoglycemia Detection in People With Diabetes Using Smartwatch Data (Lehmann et al.) - context only (classification)
findings.summary: 22 insulin-treated adults, Garmin vivoactive 4S + Empatica E4 + CGM; ML applied to unseen individuals; hypoglycaemia (<3.9 mmol/L) AUROC 0.76 +/- 0.07 from wearable data alone (HR up, HRV down, tonic EDA up). Not regression.
findings.relevance_to_our_paper: Demonstrates the realistic ceiling for wrist wearables without calibration is event detection via autonomic correlates, not glucose regression; supports our Discussion framing.

implications: The core message ('random splits leak; zone A+B is uninformative; mean baseline matches models') has already been published in preprint form by Ramesh et al. (arXiv:2608.01820, Aug 2026) on VitalDB + the same Mendeley recordings, with a public pipeline. 'Ground-breaking' is not defensible; the paper is publishable only if it is explicitly positioned as adding four things they lack: (1) discovery and automated test for the label-replication artefact in the Kaggle clean-dataset.csv derivative, (2) LOSO on the raw Mendeley recordings with recording-level aggregation, (3) a within-subject chronological protocol with a 1-h guard gap on wearable BVP vs CGM (BIG IDEAs) against a subject-mean null, (4) a controlled negative result for 1D/2D/3D multi-view fusion vs a 1-D CNN. Related Work must cite Ramesh et al. in the first paragraph and the Introduction must not claim priority for the leakage argument.

synthesize.frank_assessment:
NO: this is not ground-breaking work and it will not be accepted at an IEEE Transactions as it stands. Verified today: the paper's central message (random/window splits inflate PPG->glucose; a mean predictor matches every model under subject-wise evaluation; Clarke A+B is uninformative without a null) was published independently by three groups between Aug and Oct 2026: Ramesh et al., arXiv:2608.01820 (3 Aug 2026; VitalDB 4,626 participants + the SAME Mendeley/MUST 23-subject recordings as OOD test; mean-baseline MAE 16.0 on MUST; code released), Seyedebrahimi et al., medRxiv 10.64898/2026.08.03.26359550 (BIG IDEAs v1.1.2, 15 subjects, subject-grouped CV; wrist-only RMSE 22.58 vs time-of-day 22.63 vs train-mean 22.76; code github.com/mirmehdi/physiofusion), and Shen et al., NeurIPS 2026 workshop poster (neurips.cc/virtual/2026/162809; 3 datasets, RTTS/STTS/PAS/LSPO/OOD, CEG 97-100% A+B even when R2 <= 0). None is cited; a reviewer will find all three in one search and treat contributions 2-4 as confirmatory.

What remains genuinely new (and is enough for a credible benchmark/methods paper, not a headline-result paper): (1) the label-replication/cross-join artefact in the Kaggle derivative 'clean-dataset.csv' (uploader muhammadyasirsaleem; local file 46,758,588 bytes; header PPG_Signal,Patient_Id,...,Glucose_level,...,pl where 'pl' is the cycling label index) - no source found documents it, and it is a label-construction leak outside Kapoor & Narayanan's 8-type taxonomy; (2) LOSO on the raw Mendeley recordings with recording-level aggregation, multi-seed networks and null/demographic/feature baselines (Ramesh only used MUST as an OOD test set); (3) the within-subject chronological protocol with a 1-h training-side guard gap on raw BVP windows against each subject's own mean (Seyedebrahimi forecast with CGM history under subject-grouped CV); (4) the 1D/2D-CWT/3D-Takens single-branch vs cross-attention fusion ablation under LOSO; (5) a measured leakage ladder on the same data (already half-run locally: Mendeley window-level 1-D CNN r 0.67 / MAE 10.3 / zone A 92.5 vs record-level r 0.23-0.34 vs LOSO r 0.32 / MAE 13.4; the record-level 'leaky subject mean' is actually WORSE, MAE 17.8, because 12/23 subjects have <=2 recordings - i.e. on this dataset window-neighbour leakage, not identity leakage, is the inflating mechanism, which is a citable nuance).

State of the draft vs the repo: the repo is ahead of the text. results/bootstrap_ci.json already holds subject-cluster bootstrap CIs (1-D CNN vs train-mean dMAE -1.4 [-3.0, +0.0], p_better 0.97; fusion -0.1 [-1.5, +1.2]; on BIG IDEAs every PPG model is significantly WORSE than the subject mean: 1-D +1.7 [+0.5, +3.1]) and results_macros.tex carries them, but the paper never uses them and still says 'statistically indistinguishable' without a test. The fusion run on BIG IDEAs has completed (within_fusion_seed0: MAE 16.68, RMSE 23.52, MARD 14.0%, r 0.25, zone A 75.9% vs null 15.28) so the empty Table II row can be filled. ResNet1D/CNN-LSTM/GBM LOSO baselines and both leakage ladders are mid-run. The 1-D CNN's 'signal' is fragile: 3-seed CI touches zero, one seed out of three is nominally significant, r=0.32 is driven by 4/67 recordings >140 mg/dL (two single 183 mg/dL readings), and the LOSO train-mean's r is -0.59 (hidden as '--' in Table I; known LOO distributional bias).

Factual/citation errors that alone would sink an IEEE submission (all verified locally or on the dataset pages today): Mendeley dataset is by Ali Kermani & Hossein Esmaeili, Univ. of Science and Technology of Mazandaran (v3 doi:10.17632/37pm7jk7jn.3, 19 Jul 2023; v4 .4, 10 Sep 2025), not 'D. Kumar, V. Kumar, S. Chaudhary'; the loader reads .csv signals under 'archive (2)/PPG_Dataset' (v3/v4 layout) while the bib cites v1; sex is 15 M / 8 F (draft: 7 F / 16 M); ages 22-61 from label files (dataset paper says 20-61); the '68 label files vs 67 signals' discrepancy is Labels/Total.csv, a concatenation of all 67 labels, not an orphan recording; BIG IDEAs Demographics.csv gives 10 F / 6 M, HbA1c 5.3-6.4 (draft says '16 adults', HbA1c 5.2-6.4; PhysioNet's 'post-menopausal females only' is contradicted by the file); PhysioNet's required citation is Cho, Kim, Bent, Dunn (v1.1.3, 13 Apr 2026), not 'Bent, Cho, Wittmann'; Bent et al. 2021 npj Digit Med (LOPO RMSE 21.22, MAPE 14.33%; personalised 21.10 / 13.26%) is not cited although it is the cohort's source paper; dinh2022ppg and li2020ecg are unverifiable/misattributed; hina2021noninvasive is a NIR-spectroscopy review; 'judging by its column layout, for other published models' has no supporting citation - every peer-reviewed paper on this cohort used the raw Mendeley files; the text says BIG IDEAs windows come from 'the 10 s before the reading' but load_bigideas takes the last two gap-free 5-s windows anywhere in a 60-s lookback; tests/test_integrity.py::test_clean_dataset_csv_is_a_cross_join reads only 20,000 rows of one patient, not the whole file as Sec. III-B claims.

Design gaps a Transactions reviewer will not waive: the BIG IDEAs comparison gives the null model subject identity (own train-period mean) while the networks are one un-personalised population model - a structural handicap, so 'no PPG model recovers any excursion' is a statement about the design (within-subject r median 0.04 is computed but unreported; between-subject r of per-subject mean predictions is +0.5); no personalised/residual arm; single seed on BIG IDEAs; no positive control showing the pipeline can learn anything; no reference-noise floor (Accu-Chek Active ISO 15197 +/-15 mg/dL or 15%; Dexcom G6 MARD 9.0-9.9%, lag 3.7 +/- 3.1 min) although the null's MARD (12.8%) is within ~4 points of the reference's own error; no hypo/hyper event sensitivity (0/68 and 0/150 detected); 5-s per-window z-scored, 0.5-8 Hz representation discards DC/perfusion, vasomotion and HRV, so the negative result is conditional on preprocessing never ablated; fusion-vs-1D 'hurts' is confounded by 3.6x parameters and one shared untuned config; title promises a quantity ('how much information') that n=23+16 euglycaemic subjects cannot deliver.

Bottom line: as-is, reject at TBME/JBHI/TIM and likely major revision-to-reject at Sensors J. With the MUST list below (cite and position against the three 2026 papers; personalised arm + 3 seeds + CIs on BIG IDEAs; positive control; finished leakage ladder incl. the derivative-CSV rung; published-architecture and frozen foundation-model probes under the same protocol; noise floors/Parkes/event metrics; corrected facts; retitle as an artefact + leakage-ladder + reporting-protocol benchmark), it becomes a solid, honest reference paper that fits IEEE JBHI (14 pp), IEEE Access (scope names negative results) or Physiological Measurement (benchmarking track; needs a pre-submission note on the 30-subject rule unless STUBA/PhysioCGM are added, which lifts finger-PPG subjects to 47). Adding one diabetic wrist-PPG cohort (PhysioCGM, 10 T1D, E4 + CGM) is what would move it from 'confirmatory' to 'the first leakage-controlled diabetic wrist-PPG result'.
best_venue_ranked: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics (JBHI) - only realistic IEEE Transactions-level home, and only AFTER the must-list refactor: 14-page limit incl. supplement (mandatory overlength charges beyond 8 pp), accepts n=21 PPG-glucose DL studies (Ali et al. 2024, doi:10.1109/JBHI.2024.3464098) so small n is not disqualifying; it is the topical home of the positive multi-view claims (Chen et al. 2024 MvCFT doi:10.1109/JBHI.2024.3351867) the paper refutes; ~14.9% acceptance; frame the harness + ladder + integrity tests as a reusable benchmark, not a null.

IEEE Access - the only IEEE venue whose written scope names 'negative results'; direct precedent Costa et al. 2023 (PPG-BP, demographics-only regressor matches intra-subject models, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3284458); no subject-count threshold; ~20% stated acceptance; 4-6 weeks to publication; APC. Best choice if speed/certainty beats prestige, and the fallback if JBHI rejects.

Physiological Measurement (IOP) - best written scope fit ('Benchmarking existing algorithms', 'rigorous validation of existing methods', standards/guidelines; <=8000 words; code/data encouraged); obstacle is the 30+ human subjects per group rule - send a pre-submission enquiry citing the methodology precedent (Suzen 2026, n=14, doi:10.1088/1361-6579/aeb8de) or add STUBA ePPG (24 subj) so finger-PPG subjects total 47. The artefact report alone could go as a Note (<=3500 words).

IEEE Sensors Journal - exact-genre precedent (Yoshizawa, Yamamoto, Ohtsuki 2023, data leakage in PPG/ECG BP estimation, doi:10.1109/JSEN.2023.3272921) and routine PPG-glucose papers, but 8-page cap, $175/page overlength, and the paper has no sensor/hardware contribution; moderate fit.

IEEE Open Journal of Engineering in Medicine and Biology (OJEMB) - fast pre-review, EMBS reviewer pool, Science format ~3000 words + 4000-word supplement, 14-page cap, US$2160 APC; forces artefact + benchmark into a short paper with the harness in supplement.

Scientific Reports (Nature Portfolio) - the sister-field pitfall papers live here (Mehta et al. 2024 PPG-BP doi:10.1038/s41598-024-68862-1; Fritzsche & Senner 2026 doi:10.1038/s41598-026-66882-7); no length limit; APC; not an IEEE venue.

npj Digital Medicine - only as a <=1200-word Matters Arising on Bent et al. 2021 (doi:10.1038/s41746-021-00465-w) reporting that on the same 16 subjects, under a chronological split with guard gap, no BVP-only model beats each subject's own mean; BIG IDEAs part only.

IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering (TBME) - 'novel engineering methods with demonstrated biomedical significance', 8-page regular papers, ~19% acceptance; takes evaluation critiques only at review/meta-analysis scale (Cheung et al. 2024, 70-study wearable-BP meta-analysis, doi:10.1109/TBME.2024.3434344); poor fit for a 23+16-subject benchmark.

IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement (TIM) - stated desk-reject criteria explicitly cover 'rely only on existing datasets' and 'algorithms without showing they improve measurement performance'; do not submit.

Add baselines: time-of-day-only (ridge on sin/cos of hour), persistence (last training-period value) and, for the forecasting framing, last CGM value. Run seeds 0 1 2 and cuts at 50/60/70/80% (chronological_split train_frac). experiments.name: Positive controls under the identical pipeline and protocols
experiments.why: A negative-result paper must show the pipeline can learn something; otherwise 'no model beats the mean' is indistinguishable from 'pipeline broken' (reviewers 2-3; Blanc et al. 2026 and NERVE-ML make this standard).
experiments.how: Same 5-s / 64 Hz / z-scored windows, same 1-D CNN and fusion net, same LOSO (Mendeley) and chronological-with-guard (BIG IDEAs): regress (a) heart rate (Welch peak, computable from the window itself - must be recoverable, target r>0.9), (b) age and sex from Mendeley labels under LOSO (weak but non-zero expected), (c) subject identity under the record-level split (classification accuracy >> 1/23), (d) a subject-level label-permutation control (shuffle glucose across subjects, keep windows) that must return to the null, and (e) a white-noise-input control (Blanc et al.). experiments.name: Add a third (and diabetic) cohort: STUBA ePPG and PhysioCGM
experiments.why: Both current cohorts are non-diabetic (Mendeley status not stated; BIG IDEAs HbA1c 5.3-6.4), n=23+16 cannot support a population claim, and Physiological Measurement requires 30+ subjects. STUBA ePPG (24 subj incl. 3 T1DM, 125 records, 3 wavelengths, 6 MB, CC0, zenodo 21308262) gives a cheap second LOSO replication and a per-wavelength ablation; PhysioCGM (10 T1D adults, 17 days, Empatica E4 + Zephyr + CGM; Sci Data 2025 doi:10.1038/s41597-025-06090-6; figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.28136294) is the only open diabetic wrist-PPG/CGM set and would make this the first leakage-controlled diabetic wrist-PPG result.
experiments.how: STUBA: write a loader (100 Hz, 30-s records, mmol/L -> mg/dL), reuse the Mendeley harness (LOSO, recording-level, train-mean null, ridge, 1-D, fusion, foundation probes), run green/red/IR separately and fused. PhysioCGM: port scripts/fetch_bigideas.py to its raw E4 BVP + cgm.csv layout (same 64 Hz E4 / 5-min CGM), run the identical chronological-with-guard protocol, subject-mean null, personalised arm; report hypo/hyper event sensitivity where glucose actually varies. Verify licence on download (sweep reports CC0; figshare blocked automated fetch).
experiments.compute_estimate: STUBA: download 6 MB, LOSO all models x 3 seeds ~ 25 min. PhysioCGM: download ~9 GB raw (hours, background), extraction ~5 min, 1-D/ridge ~5 min, fusion ~15 min per seed; ~1 h compute.
experiments.data_needed: Downloads: zenodo.org/records/21308262 (stuba_ppg_bgl_dataset.zip, 5.9 MB) and figshare 28136294 raw zips (10 x ~1 GB).

experiments.name: Hyper-parameter fairness and capacity control for the fusion-vs-1D claim
experiments.why: 'Adding the 2-D and 3-D views hurts' is confounded by 3.6x parameters and one shared untuned config (lr 1e-3, 40 epochs, bs 16); the Limitations concede it but Results/Abstract assert it.
experiments.how: Nested, leakage-safe sweep inside training folds (inner GroupKFold by subject) over lr {3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3}, weight decay {1e-4, 1e-2}, epochs {20, 40, 80} for 1-D and fusion; add a capacity-matched 1-D (widen channels to ~550k params), a late-fusion average of the three single branches, and a frozen-branch probe (train branches alone, ridge on concatenated embeddings). Report fusion-minus-1D with cluster-bootstrap CI; reword to 'under the configurations tested' if the CI includes zero.
experiments.compute_estimate: 1-D: 18 configs x ~4 min x 3 seeds ~ 3.5 h; fusion: 18 x ~8 min x 3 ~ 7 h. Run overnight in the researcher's terminal (or reduce to 6 configs each, ~3 h).

experiments.name: Reproduce the inflation inside Ramesh et al.'s released pipeline using the Kaggle derivative
experiments.why: Creates a direct, citable link between the artefact and the strongest concurrent paper: shows that even their participant-aware/LSPO protocol is defeated by the label-construction leak (subject-wise splitting cannot detect it).
experiments.how: Clone github.com/R-Supraja/bgl-evaluation-pipeline into an isolated directory; feed windows cut from clean-dataset.csv as a 'dataset' with participant IDs; run their 1D-CNN and feature+XGBoost under their participant-aware split; show MAE/zone A near the oracle and R2 inflated vs the raw-recording run. Also run their pipeline on the raw Mendeley recordings to reproduce their MUST mean-baseline MAE 16.0 / zone A 77.6% as an external check of our train-mean row.
experiments.compute_estimate: Setup 1-2 h of engineering; runs ~20-30 min on CPU/MPS.
experiments.data_needed: clean-dataset.csv and raw Mendeley (on disk); their repo.

experiments.name: VitalDB leave-some-participants-out scale-up of the 1-D CNN and fusion net
experiments.why: Scales the cross-subject null from 23 to thousands of subjects with the same architecture; Ramesh et al. provide the reference numbers (mean baseline MAE 26.4, ResNet-34 LSPO MAE 25.9, R2 -0.04).
experiments.how: Use the vitaldb Python API to pull PLETH + preop_gluc / lab glucose for a subset (e.g. 1,000 cases, 10-s windows within +/-8 min of a glucose label, 500 Hz -> 64 Hz), 5-fold grouped by patient, train-mean null, 1-D CNN, fusion, foundation probes; acknowledge anaesthesia confound.
experiments.compute_estimate: Download 1,000 cases ~1-2 h; views ~10 min; 1-D 5-fold ~15 min; fusion ~2 h. Researcher's terminal.
experiments.data_needed: VitalDB (open, CC BY 4.0; physionet.org/content/vitaldb/1.0.0 or api.vitaldb.net).

experiments.how: Download zenodo.org/records/20577959 (3.5 GB), adapt loader (64 Hz PPG, 15-min CGM), run the BIG IDEAs protocol with subject-mean null; complete TRIPOD+AI (items 5a, 10, 12a/c/d/e, 18e/f, 23a) and PROBAST+AI self-assessment, and rate the criticised prior papers (Zeynali 2025, Soliman 2024, Chu 2021, Syamsul & Kim 2026) on PROBAST+AI's analysis domain in a short table.
experiments.compute_estimate: Download ~1 h; runs ~10 min; checklists no compute.
